title.zh: 卷九十七下 外戚傳
title.en: Volume 97a: The Empresses and Imperial Affines 2
title.raw: 卷九十七下 外戚傳 Volume 97a: The Empresses and Imperial Affines 2

sentences.zh: 卷九十七下 外戚傳第六十七下

translations.literal: Volume 97 (second part), Biography of the Empresses and Imperial Affines, number 67 (second part).
translations.idiomatic: Book 97B: Biographies of Empresses and Imperial Affines, Part Two.

sentences.zh: 孝元王皇后

translations.literal: Empress Xiaoyuan, nee Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaoyuan of the Wang clan.

sentences.zh: 孝元王皇后，成帝母也。

translations.literal: Empress Xiaoyuan, nee Wang, was the mother of Emperor Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaoyuan of the Wang family was Emperor Cheng's mother.

sentences.zh: 家凡十侯，五大司馬，外戚莫盛焉。

translations.literal: In her house there were ten marquises in all and five grand marshals; among affines by marriage none was more exalted.
translations.idiomatic: Her kin would hold ten marquisates and five grand-marshal posts—no other imperial in-law clan ever rose so high.

sentences.zh: 自有傳。

translations.literal: She has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Her life is recounted in its own chapter.

sentences.zh: 孝成許皇后

translations.literal: Empress Xiaocheng, nee Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaocheng of the Xu clan.

sentences.zh: 孝成許皇后，大司馬車騎將軍平恩侯嘉女也。

translations.literal: Empress Xiaocheng, nee Xu, was the daughter of Grand Marshal and General of Chariots and Cavalry, Marquis of Pingen, Jia.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaocheng was the daughter of Xu Jia, grand marshal and general of chariots and cavalry, Marquis of Pingen.

sentences.zh: 元帝悼傷母恭哀後居位日淺而遭霍氏之辜，故選嘉女以配皇太子。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan grieved that his mother Empress Gong'ai had occupied her position only briefly and had suffered the crime of the Huo clan; therefore he chose Jia's daughter to match the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan still mourned how briefly his mother, Empress Gong'ai, had been empress and how she had been destroyed in the Huo purge; he therefore chose Xu Jia's daughter as consort to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 初入太了家，上令中常侍黃門親近者侍送，還白太子歡說狀，元帝喜謂左右：「酌酒賀我！

translations.literal: When she first entered the crown prince's household, the sovereign ordered intimate attendants among the regular palace attendants and yellow-gate officials to escort and serve her; when they returned and reported how pleased the heir apparent was, Emperor Yuan joyfully said to those around him, 'Pour wine and congratulate me!'
translations.idiomatic: On her first arrival at the crown prince's residence, the emperor sent trusted eunuchs from the inner court to attend her; when they reported back how delighted the heir was, Yuan told his attendants, 'Bring wine—I must be congratulated!'

sentences.zh: 」左右皆稱萬歲。

translations.literal: Those around him all cried 'ten thousand years.'
translations.idiomatic: The whole company shouted long life.

sentences.zh: 久之，有一男，失之。

translations.literal: After a long time, she had one son, and lost him.
translations.idiomatic: Time passed, and she bore a son who died in infancy.

sentences.zh: 乃成帝即位，立許妃為皇后，復生一女，失之。

translations.literal: Then when Emperor Cheng ascended the throne, he established Consort Xu as empress; she bore another daughter, and lost her.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng took the throne he raised Consort Xu to empress; she gave birth again, to a daughter who did not survive.

sentences.zh: 妾誇布服糲糧，加以幼稚愚惑，不明義理，幸得免離茅屋之下，備後宮掃除。

translations.literal: Your servant came up from coarse cloth and coarse grain; moreover childish, foolish, and confused, not understanding right principle—yet by fortune I was spared leaving life beneath a thatched hut and was appointed to sweep and cleanse the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: I was raised on plain cloth and coarse food; I was young and foolish and barely grasped how one ought to behave—yet I was lifted out of a humble cottage and given a place among the women who serve in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 蒙過誤之寵，居非命所當托，污穢不修，曠職屍官，數逆至法，逾越制度，當伏放流之誅，不足以塞責。

translations.literal: Receiving erroneous excessive favor, occupying what fate ought not to entrust to me, failing to cleanse filth, neglecting office and occupying rank as a corpse, repeatedly violating the utmost law and transgressing regulations—I deserve exile or execution and cannot make good my guilt.
translations.idiomatic: I accepted honors beyond my deserts and held a station beyond what Heaven intended; I let duty lapse and occupied office like the dead; again and again I broke the law and overstepped the rules—I merit banishment or death, and no punishment could square my account.

sentences.zh: 乃壬寅日大長秋受詔：「椒房儀法，御服輿駕，所發諸官署，及所造作，遺賜外家群臣妾，皆如竟寧以前故事。

translations.literal: Then on the renyin day the grand chief of the long autumn received an edict: 'The protocol of the pepper chambers, imperial dress, chariots, and what is issued from the various offices, and what is manufactured, and gifts to the empress's kin, ministers, and your servant's concubines—all are to follow the precedents of before the Jingning era.'
translations.idiomatic: On the day renyin the head eunuch brought an edict: 'Ritual in the empress's quarters, imperial wardrobe, carriages, requisitions from every office, new work orders, and gifts to my family and the officials—all must follow the practice in force before the Jingning period.'

sentences.zh: 」妾伏自念，入椒房以來，遺賜外家未嘗逾故事，每輒決上，可復問也。

translations.literal: Your servant prostrates herself and reflects: since entering the pepper chambers, gifts to the empress's kin have never exceeded precedent; each time it was decided by the sovereign—this can be asked about again.
translations.idiomatic: I have considered this carefully: from the day I entered the empress's residence, every gift to my family stayed within precedent, and the sovereign decided each one—it can all be checked again in the records.

sentences.zh: 今誠時世異制，長短相補，不出漢制而已，纖微之間，未必可同。

translations.literal: Now truly the times differ and systems differ; long and short complement one another, and it is only a matter of not departing from Han institutions—yet in the finest details, they need not be identical.
translations.idiomatic: Times change and so do the rules; one regime patches another, but all still sit inside Han law—only the small points cannot always be matched line for line.

sentences.zh: 若竟寧前與黃龍前，豈相放哉？

translations.literal: As for before Jingning and before Huanglong—can they be modeled on each other?
translations.idiomatic: How could the era before Jingning simply be copied from the age before Huanglong?

sentences.zh: 家吏不曉，今一受詔如此，且使妾搖手不得。

translations.literal: The household clerks do not understand; now, having once received an edict like this, it moreover makes it so your servant cannot even wave a hand.
translations.idiomatic: My staff do not know how to read this; with one such order they have tied my hands so I can hardly move.

sentences.zh: 今言無得發取諸官，殆謂未央官不屬妾，不宜獨取也。

translations.literal: Now saying one may not issue requisitions from the various offices—perhaps it means Weiyang Palace does not belong to your servant and one ought not take solely from there.
translations.idiomatic: The ban on drawing supplies from the offices must mean Weiyang Palace is not mine alone and I should not be the only one drawing from it.

sentences.zh: 言妾家府亦不當得，妾竊惑焉。

translations.literal: Saying your servant's household treasury also ought not obtain—affects your servant's private puzzlement.
translations.idiomatic: The line that my private storehouse may not receive either leaves me quite at a loss.

sentences.zh: 幸得賜湯沐邑以自奉養，亦小發取其中，何害於誼而不可哉？

translations.literal: Since I have by fortune been granted a bath-and-wash fief to support myself, to make small requisitions from it as well—what harm to right conduct, and why may it not be done?
translations.idiomatic: I have been given a fief for my maintenance; to take a little from that for my needs—where is the impropriety, and why should it be forbidden?

sentences.zh: 又詔書言服御所造，皆如竟寧前，吏誠不能揆其意，即且令妾被服所為不得不如前。

translations.literal: Moreover the edict says that what is made for dress and use shall all be as before Jingning—the clerks truly cannot fathom its intent, and they thereupon order your servant's clothing and conduct not to fail to be as before.
translations.idiomatic: The edict also says garments and equipage must match pre-Jingning standards; the clerks cannot divine what that means, so they demand my dress and every commission mirror the old models exactly.

sentences.zh: 設妾欲作某屏風張於某所，曰故事無有，或不能得，則必繩妾以詔書矣。

translations.literal: Suppose your servant wishes to make a certain screen and hang it in a certain place, and it is said there is no precedent, or it cannot be obtained—then they are sure to bind your servant with the edict.
translations.idiomatic: If I want a certain screen in a certain hall and they say there is no precedent or the materials cannot be had, they will prosecute me for defying the edict.

sentences.zh: 此二事誠不可行，唯陛下省察。

translations.literal: These two matters truly cannot be carried out; I beg Your Majesty to examine them.
translations.idiomatic: These two points are simply unworkable; I beg you to look into them yourself.

sentences.zh: 宦吏忮佷，必欲自勝。

translations.literal: Eunuch clerks are jealous and cruel; they are determined to prevail.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch officials are spiteful and harsh; each one must win at any cost.

sentences.zh: 幸妾尚貴時，猶以不急事操人，況今日日益侵，又獲此詔，其操約人，豈有所訴？

translations.literal: Fortunately when your servant was still honored, they still used people on matters that were not urgent; how much more now, with encroachment growing day by day, and having received this edict—when they restrain people, is there any place to appeal?
translations.idiomatic: When I still had standing they would harp on trifles; now my position shrinks by the day and this edict gives them a whip—when they tighten every leash, whom could I possibly petition?

sentences.zh: 陛下見妾在椒房，終不肯給妾纖微內邪？

translations.literal: Does Your Majesty see your servant in the pepper chambers and to the end refuse to grant your servant the slightest thing within?
translations.idiomatic: Because I sit in the empress's quarters, will you never grant me even the smallest provision from within the palace?

sentences.zh: 若不私府小取，將安所仰乎？

translations.literal: If one does not take a little from the private treasury, upon what will one rely?
translations.idiomatic: If I may not draw even modestly on my private stores, what am I to live on?

sentences.zh: 舊故，中官乃私奪左右之賤繒，乃發乘輿服繒，言為待詔補，已而貿易其中。

translations.literal: By old practice, palace insiders privately seized cheap silk from attendants, then issued imperial-train silk, saying it was to mend things for awaiting-edict attendants, and afterward traded within it.
translations.idiomatic: By long habit inner-court men seize cheap silk from servants, then order fabric meant for the emperor's wardrobe, claim it is for patching gentlemen-in-waiting's robes, and sell the surplus on the side.

sentences.zh: 左右多竊怨者，甚恥為之。

translations.literal: Many of those around secretly resented it and were greatly ashamed to do it.
translations.idiomatic: The attendants nursed secret resentment and were deeply ashamed to take part.

sentences.zh: 又故事以特牛祠大父母，戴侯、敬侯皆得蒙恩以太牢祠，今當率如故事，唯陛下哀之！

translations.literal: Moreover by precedent a single bull was used to sacrifice to great-grandparents; Marquis Dai and Marquis Jing both received favor to sacrifice with the greater victim—now it ought universally to follow precedent; I beg Your Majesty's pity!
translations.idiomatic: Precedent allowed a bull for offerings to my grandparents; both Marquis Dai and Marquis Jing were honored with full taishao sacrifices—let that practice stand; I beg your compassion!

sentences.zh: 今吏甫受詔讀記，直豫言使後知之，非可復若私府有所取也。

translations.literal: Now the clerks have just received the edict and read the record, and straightaway announce in advance to let posterity know—it cannot again be as when the private treasury had something to take.
translations.idiomatic: The clerks have barely finished reading the edict aloud and already proclaim it for the record, as if to bind the future—there can be no repeat of the old informal draws from my treasury.

sentences.zh: 其萌牙所以約制妾者，恐失人理。

translations.literal: The sprouting by which they intend to restrain your servant—perhaps it loses human principle.
translations.idiomatic: This first tightening of the reins on me seems to me inhuman.

sentences.zh: 今但損車駕，及毋若未央官有所發，遺賜衣服如故事，則可矣。

translations.literal: Now only reduce chariots and horses, and do not let Weiyang Palace issue anything; gifts of clothing as in precedent—then it can be acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: If you only trim the carriage establishment, forbid new issues from Weiyang, and keep gifts of clothing on the old footing, that would be enough.

sentences.zh: 其餘誠太迫急，奈何？

translations.literal: As for the rest, it is truly too pressing and harsh—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: The rest is simply too harsh—what am I to do?

sentences.zh: 妾薄命，端遇竟寧前，竟寧前於今世而比之，豈可邪？

translations.literal: Your servant has a thin fate; she happens to meet before Jingning; before Jingning compared to the present age—can it be the same?
translations.idiomatic: I am ill-starred: my life straddles the world before Jingning and the world after—how can the two be judged by the same measure?

sentences.zh: 故時酒肉有所賜外家，輒上表乃決。

translations.literal: In former times when wine and meat were granted to the empress's kin, always a memorial went up and then it was decided.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly every gift of wine or meat to my family required a memorial to you before it went forward.

sentences.zh: 又故杜陵梁美人歲時遺酒一石，肉百斤耳。

translations.literal: Moreover formerly Lady Liang of Duling at the seasonal observances sent wine one shi and meat one hundred jin only.
translations.idiomatic: Even Lady Liang of Duling at festival time sent only one shi of wine and a hundred jin of meat.

sentences.zh: 妾甚少之，遺田八子誠不可若是。

translations.literal: Your servant thought that very meager; in giving to Lady Tian Bazi, it truly cannot be like this.
translations.idiomatic: I found that allowance paltry; gifts to Lady Tian Bazi cannot in good conscience be cut to the same measure.

sentences.zh: 事率眾多，不可勝以文陳。

translations.literal: Matters are numerous in general and cannot all be set forth in writing.
translations.idiomatic: There are countless particulars that no memorial could hold.

sentences.zh: 俟自見，索言之，唯陛下深察焉！

translations.literal: Wait until you see for yourself, then seek to speak of them—I beg Your Majesty to examine deeply!
translations.idiomatic: When we meet face to face I will lay them out; I implore you to consider them with care.

sentences.zh: 上於是采劉向、谷永之言以報曰：

translations.literal: Thereupon the sovereign adopted the words of Liu Xiang and Gu Yong and replied, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then drew on what Liu Xiang and Gu Yong had said and answered:

sentences.zh: 皇帝向皇后，所言事聞之。

translations.literal: The emperor faces the empress: what was spoken has been heard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor to the empress: we have heard everything you said.

sentences.zh: 夫日者眾陽之宗，天光之貴，王者之象，人君之位也。

translations.literal: Now the sun is the ancestor of all yang, the nobility of heaven's radiance, the image of the king, and the position of the lord of men.
translations.idiomatic: The sun is sovereign among the yang forces, the supreme light of Heaven, the emblem of kingship and of the ruler's throne.

sentences.zh: 夫以陰而侵陽，虧其正體，是非下陵上，妻乘夫，賤逾貴之變與？

translations.literal: For yin to encroach on yang and injure its correct substance—is this not the transformation of the inferior overawing the superior, the wife riding the husband, the base exceeding the noble?
translations.idiomatic: When yin encroaches on yang and mars its true form, is that not the omen of subjects lording it over the throne, wives dominating husbands, the lowly overwhelming their betters?

sentences.zh: 春秋二百四十二年，變異為眾，莫若日蝕大。

translations.literal: In the two hundred forty-two years of the Spring and Autumn period, anomalies were many; none was greater than eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Across the Spring and Autumn's two hundred forty-two years Heaven sent many prodigies; none counted for more than a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 自漢興，日蝕亦為呂、霍之屬見。

translations.literal: Since Han rose, solar eclipses have also appeared for the likes of the Lü and Huo.
translations.idiomatic: Since our dynasty began, eclipses have heralded crises such as those of the Lü clan and the Huo clan.

sentences.zh: 以今揆之，豈有此等之效與？

translations.literal: Measured by the present, could there be effects of this sort?
translations.idiomatic: Judged by today's court, do we really face anything on that scale?

sentences.zh: 諸侯拘迫漢制，牧相執持之也，又安獲齊、趙七國之難？

translations.literal: The feudal lords were constrained and pressed by Han institutions; shepherds and chancellors held them in check—how then could the disaster of the seven states of Qi and Zhao have been gotten?
translations.idiomatic: The kingdoms were hemmed in by Han law and held fast by regional governors—how could we again see a rebellion like the seven kingdoms of Qi and Zhao?

sentences.zh: 將相大臣懷誠秉忠，唯義是從，又惡有上官、博陸、宣成之謀？

translations.literal: Generals, ministers, and great officials embrace sincerity and uphold loyalty; they follow only righteousness—how could there be plots like those of Shangguan, Bolu, and Xuancheng?
translations.idiomatic: Our generals and ministers are loyal men who heed duty alone—where would we find another coup like those of the Shangguan, Huo, or Xuancheng factions?

sentences.zh: 若乃徒步豪桀，非有陳勝、項梁之群也；

translations.literal: As for foot-traveling heroes, there are not bands like those of Chen Sheng and Xiang Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Among common-born adventurers there is no host of Chen Shengs and Xiang Liangs.

sentences.zh: 匈奴、夷狄，非有冒頓、郅支之倫也。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu and the barbarians are not of the class of Modun and Zhizhi.
translations.idiomatic: On the steppe there is no new Modun or Zhizhi to fear.

sentences.zh: 方外內鄉，百蠻賓服，殊俗慕義，八州懷德，雖使其懷挾邪意，狄不足憂，又況其無乎？

translations.literal: Those beyond the bounds turn inward; the hundred Man submit as guests; alien customs admire righteousness; the eight provinces cherish virtue—even supposing they harbor wicked intent, the Di are not worth worry; how much more when there is none?
translations.idiomatic: The border peoples incline toward us, the tribes pay homage, distant customs admire our rightness, and the heartland rests in our benevolence—even if malice stirred abroad, the barbarians would hardly threaten us, let alone when they do not.

sentences.zh: 求於夷狄無有，求於臣下無有，微後官也當，何以塞之？

translations.literal: Seeking among the barbarians there is nothing; seeking among ministers and subordinates there is nothing—if it is the subtle rear palace that is appropriate, what will fill it?
translations.idiomatic: We find no fault in the frontier peoples nor among the officials; if the blame lies only with the inner palace, how else can we answer Heaven's warning?

sentences.zh: 日者，建始元年正月，白氣出於營室。

translations.literal: Recently, in the first month of the first year of Jianshi, white vapor issued from Encampment Chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago, in the first month of Jianshi 1 (32 BCE), a white emanation appeared in the Encampment constellation.

sentences.zh: 營室者，天子之後官也。

translations.literal: Encampment Chamber is the Son of Heaven's rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: That mansion stands for the emperor's inner palace.

sentences.zh: 正月於《尚書》為皇極。

translations.literal: The first month in the Documents is 'august summit.'
translations.idiomatic: The first month is called huangji—'royal perfection'—in the Documents.

sentences.zh: 皇極者，王氣之極也。

translations.literal: 'August summit' is the utmost of kingly qi.
translations.idiomatic: Huangji marks the pinnacle of the sovereign's vital force.

sentences.zh: 白者西方之氣，其於春當廢。

translations.literal: White is the qi of the west; in spring it ought to be discarded.
translations.idiomatic: White belongs to the western element and should wither in spring.

sentences.zh: 今正於皇極之月，興廢氣於後宮，視後妾無能懷任保全者，以著繼嗣之微，賤人將起也。

translations.literal: Now precisely in the month of august summit, raising discarded qi in the rear palace, showing that rear concubines have none able to conceive and preserve—it manifests the faintness of heirs; base persons will arise.
translations.idiomatic: Now, in the very month that ought to crown royal fortune, a dying western vapor rises over the harem, showing no consort can carry a child safely—Heaven signals how thin the succession runs and warns that low-born rivals will rise.

sentences.zh: 至其九月，流星如瓜，出於文昌，貫紫宮，尾委曲如龍，臨於鉤陳，此又章顯前尤，著在內也。

translations.literal: Down to its ninth month, a meteor like a melon emerged from Literary Glory, pierced Purple Palace, its tail twisting like a dragon, looming over Hook Array—this again openly displays the earlier fault, manifest within.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn a melon-sized meteor burst from the Wenchang stars, streaked through the Purple Forbidden enclosure, trailed like a dragon over Gouchen—another blazing advertisement that the earlier guilt sits inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 其後則有北宮井溢，南流逆理，數郡水出，流殺人民。

translations.literal: After that there was the Northern Palace well overflowing, flowing south contrary to principle, water issuing in several commanderies, the flow killing the people.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Northern Palace well burst and poured south against nature; floods broke out across whole commanderies and drowned the populace.

sentences.zh: 後則訛言傳相驚震，女童入殿，鹹莫覺知。

translations.literal: Afterward false reports circulated and mutually alarmed; a girl child entered the hall and none perceived.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors flew from mouth to mouth in panic; a little girl walked into the hall and no guard noticed.

sentences.zh: 夫河者水陰，四瀆之長，今乃大決，沒漂陵邑，斯昭陰盛盈溢，違經絕紀之應也。

translations.literal: Now the Yellow River is water-yin, chief of the four channels; now it has greatly burst forth, submerging and sweeping mausoleum towns—this illuminates yin flourishing and overflowing, the response of violating the classics and cutting off the threads.
translations.idiomatic: The river is yin among waters and head of the four great streams; its breach now swamps imperial tomb districts—a plain sign that yin has flooded its banks and broken every norm Heaven set.

sentences.zh: 乃昔之月，鼠巢於樹，野鵲變色。

translations.literal: In the same month, rats nested in trees; wild magpies changed color.
translations.idiomatic: That same month rats built nests in treetops and wild magpies changed their plumage.

sentences.zh: 五月庚子，鳥焚其巢太山之域。

translations.literal: On gengzi of the fifth month, birds burned their nests in the region of Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi in the fifth month birds immolated their own nests on Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「鳥焚其巢，旅人先笑後號啕。

translations.literal: The Changes say: 'The bird burns its nest; the wayfarer first laughs, afterward wails and cries.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes reads: 'The bird burns its nest; the traveler first laughs, then breaks into tears.'

sentences.zh: 喪牛於易，凶。

translations.literal: 'Loses the ox in the easy field—inauspicious.'
translations.idiomatic: He loses his ox in the open meadow—ill omen.

sentences.zh: 」言王者處民上，如鳥之處巢也，不顧恤百姓，百姓畔而去之，若鳥之自焚也，雖先快意說笑，其後必號而無及也。

translations.literal: It means the king who stands above the people is like a bird in its nest; if he does not look with pity on the hundred surnames, the hundred surnames will revolt and leave him, as if the bird burned itself; though at first pleased and laughing happily, afterward they are sure to wail too late.
translations.idiomatic: That pictures the ruler perched above the folk like a bird on its nest: neglect the people and they slip away as surely as if the bird had set fire to its own home—there may be laughter at first, but the reckoning ends in helpless weeping.

sentences.zh: 百姓喪其君，若牛亡其毛也，故稱凶。

translations.literal: The hundred surnames lose their lord as if an ox loses its hair; therefore it is called inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: When the people lose their ruler they are as helpless as an ox stripped of its hide—hence the text names it misfortune.

sentences.zh: 泰山，王者易姓告代之處，今正於岱宗之山，甚可懼也。

translations.literal: Mount Tai is the place where kings change surname and announce succession; now precisely on Mount Dai Zong—it is greatly to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Tai is where dynasties announce the turnover of the mandate; for such a sign to appear right on the sacred summit is terrifying.

sentences.zh: 三月癸未，大風自西搖祖宗寢廟，揚裂帷席，折拔樹木，頓僵車輦，毀壞檻屋，災及宗廟，足為寒心！

translations.literal: On guiwei of the third month, a great wind from the west rocked the temples of the ancestors, lifted and tore curtains and mats, broke and uprooted trees, toppled and stiffened chariots and palanquins, destroyed railing houses; disaster reached the ancestral temples—enough to chill the heart!
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei in the third month a gale out of the west shook the imperial shrines, shredded hangings, snapped trees, overturned carriages, tore down colonnades—the ancestral temples themselves were struck; the thought chills the blood.

sentences.zh: 四月己亥，日蝕東井，轉旅且索，與既無異。

translations.literal: On jihai of the fourth month, the sun was eclipsed at Eastern Well; turning traveler and moreover rope—it differs not from total eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai in the fourth month the sun was eaten over the Eastern Well constellation—waning like a traveler exhausting his provisions, no different from a total eclipse.

sentences.zh: 己猶戊也，亥復水也，明陰盛，咎在內。

translations.literal: Ji is still wu; hai again is water—it illumines yin flourishing; blame lies within.
translations.idiomatic: The stem ji allies with earth like wu; the branch hai belongs to water—together they proclaim surging yin and fault inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 於戊己，虧君體，著絕世於皇極，顯禍敗及京都。

translations.literal: Regarding wu and ji, it injures the lord's substance; it manifests cutting off generations at the august summit; it openly shows calamity and ruin reaching the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On wu and ji days Heaven wounds the sovereign's person, threatens the succession at the throne's zenith, and brings ruin down on the capital itself.

sentences.zh: 於東井，變怪眾備，末重益大，來數益甚。

translations.literal: Regarding Eastern Well, anomalies are many and complete; the end grows heavier and larger; the coming frequency grows more severe.
translations.idiomatic: At Eastern Well every kind of prodigy gathers; each new wave weighs heavier than the last and strikes more often.

sentences.zh: 成形之禍月以迫切，不救之患日寢屢深，咎敗灼灼若此，豈可以忽哉！

translations.literal: Formed calamities press month by month; uncorrected peril daily sleeps and repeatedly deepens; blame and ruin blaze thus—how can they be neglected?
translations.idiomatic: Disaster takes shape with every turning moon; the incurable evil sinks deeper day by day—when Heaven flashes warnings this bright, no ruler dare brush them aside.

sentences.zh: 《書》云：「高宗肜日，粵有雊雉。

translations.literal: The Documents say: 'On the day after Gaozong's second sacrifice, there crowed a pheasant.'
translations.idiomatic: The Documents record: 'The day after Gaozong's offering, a wild pheasant crowed on the temple roof.'

sentences.zh: 祖己曰：『惟先假王正厥事。

translations.literal: Zu Ji said: "Only first lending the king corrects these affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ji answered: "He must first enlighten the king so that he sets his house in order."

sentences.zh: 』」又曰：「雖休勿休，惟敬五刑，以成三德。

translations.literal: Again it says: 'Though there be rest, do not rest; reverently attend to the five punishments, thereby completing the three virtues.'
translations.idiomatic: The text also says: 'Even in ease do not trust to ease; honor the five punishments until the three royal virtues are fulfilled.'

sentences.zh: 」即飭椒房及掖庭耳。

translations.literal: That is to regulate the pepper chambers and the lateral courts, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Apply that counsel to the empress's quarters and the lesser palaces—nothing more.

sentences.zh: 今皇后有所疑，便不便，其條刺，使大長秋來白之。

translations.literal: Now if the empress has doubts, convenient or inconvenient, let her itemize them and send the grand chief of the long autumn to report them.
translations.idiomatic: If you have misgivings, great or small, list them clearly and have the chief eunuch bring them to me.

sentences.zh: 吏拘於法，亦安足過？

translations.literal: The clerks are bound by law—how can they be blamed?
translations.idiomatic: The clerks are only enforcing statute—there is no cause to fault them.

sentences.zh: 蓋矯枉者過直，古今同之。

translations.literal: For straightening the bent passes straightness—past and present share this.
translations.idiomatic: Correcting a bend always swings past the mark—that has been true in every age.

sentences.zh: 且財幣之省，特牛之祠，其於皇后，所以扶助德美，為華寵也。

translations.literal: Moreover the cutting of wealth and currency, the sacrifice of a single bull—these toward the empress are means to support virtue and beauty, to be splendid favor.
translations.idiomatic: The purse-tightening and the lone bull for sacrifice are meant to shore up your moral standing and surround you with honorable favor.

sentences.zh: 咎根不除，災變相襲，祖宗且不血食，何戴侯也！

translations.literal: If the root of blame is not removed, disasters and anomalies succeed one another—ancestors will not even have blood-and-food offerings; what of Marquis Dai!
translations.idiomatic: Unless we tear out this evil at the root, omens will pile one on another until our forefathers go hungry in their shrines—what good then is a noble title like Marquis Dai?

sentences.zh: 傳不雲乎！

translations.literal: Does not the tradition say!
translations.idiomatic: Has the tradition not warned us?

sentences.zh: 「以納失之者鮮。

translations.literal: 'Those who lose by accepting are few.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Few rulers ruin themselves by listening to good counsel.'

sentences.zh: 」審皇后欲從其奢與？

translations.literal: Consider whether the empress wishes to follow extravagance?
translations.idiomatic: Tell me plainly: do you mean to cling to extravagance?

sentences.zh: 朕亦當法孝武皇帝也，如此則甘泉、建章可復興矣。

translations.literal: We too ought to model Emperor Xiaowu; if so, then Sweet Springs and Establishing Brilliance can be raised again.
translations.idiomatic: Should I emulate Martial Emperor's excesses? Then we could rebuild Sweet Springs and Establishing Brilliance palaces overnight.

sentences.zh: 世俗歲殊，時變日化，遭事制宜，因時而移，舊之非者，何可放焉！

translations.literal: Common customs differ year by year; times change and days transform; encountering affairs one sets what is fitting and shifts with the times—what was wrong in the old, how can it be modeled!
translations.idiomatic: Custom shifts every year; policy must fit the hour—the errors of former reigns are no pattern to copy.

sentences.zh: 郡子之道，樂因循而重改作。

translations.literal: The way of the princely gentleman is to delight in continuity and to give weight to reconstruction.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler who understands duty prefers steady precedent to restless rebuilding.

sentences.zh: 昔魯人為長府，閔子騫曰：「仍舊貫如之何？

translations.literal: Formerly the people of Lu worked on the Long Treasury; Min Ziqian said: 'Still the old conduit—what about it?'
translations.idiomatic: When the Lu ministers wanted to enlarge the Long Treasury, Min Ziqian asked, 'Why not keep the old vault as it is?'

sentences.zh: 何必改作！

translations.literal: 'Why must there be reconstruction!'
translations.idiomatic: 'What need is there to rip it apart and build anew?'

sentences.zh: 」蓋惡之也。

translations.literal: In general he loathed it.
translations.idiomatic: —because he despised the whole project.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「雖無老成人，尚有典刑，曾是莫聽，大命以傾。

translations.literal: The Odes say: 'Though there are no elders, still there are models and punishments; such were never heeded—the great mandate thereby toppled.'
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Poetry warns: 'Even without gray-haired ministers, the ancient precedents remain; ignore them and the mandate itself will collapse.'

sentences.zh: 」孝文皇帝，朕之師也。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen is Our teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen is my own model.

sentences.zh: 皇太后，皇后成法也。

translations.literal: The empress dowager is the empress's completed law.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager sets the standard you must live up to.

sentences.zh: 假使太后在彼時不如職，今見親厚，又惡可以逾乎！

translations.literal: Suppose the empress dowager at that time did not match office; now seeing closeness and kindness—how can one exceed!
translations.idiomatic: Even if her Majesty had fallen short of duty in those days, she shows you such kindness now—how could you presume to go beyond what she allows?

sentences.zh: 皇后其刻心秉德，毋違先後之制度，力誼勉行，稱順婦道，減省群事，謙約為右，其孝東宮，毋厥朔望，推誠永究，爰何不臧！

translations.literal: Empress, engrave this on your heart and uphold virtue; do not violate the institutions of former queens; exert yourself in righteousness and strive in conduct; accord with and comply with the way of a wife; reduce and cut back throngs of affairs; take humility and restraint as the right hand; be filial to the Eastern Palace; do not fail the new and full moons; extend sincerity and pursue it to the end—how could anything then not be good!
translations.idiomatic: Take these words to heart and live by them: honor the precedents set by your predecessors as empress; devote yourself to duty and modest wifely conduct; trim extravagance and let humility be your guide; serve the empress dowager faithfully and never miss the ritual visits at new and full moon; let good faith be your lasting rule—and what blessing could you lack?

sentences.zh: 養名顯行，以息眾言雚，垂則列妾，使有法焉。

translations.literal: Nurture reputation and display conduct, thereby stilling the multitude of clamorous words; hang down regulations for the ranked concubines, causing there to be law therein.
translations.idiomatic: Build a name through upright behavior, quiet the court's gossip, and set an example for every woman of the harem so that all may see what the law requires.

sentences.zh: 皇后深惟毋忽！

translations.literal: Empress, ponder deeply—do not neglect!
translations.idiomatic: Reflect on this carefully, empress, and do not dismiss it lightly.

sentences.zh: 是時，大將軍鳳用事，威權尤盛。

translations.literal: At this time Grand General Feng held power; his might and authority were especially great.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Wang Feng dominated the government, and his power was immense.

sentences.zh: 其後，比三年日蝕，言事者頗歸咎於鳳矣。

translations.literal: Afterward, for three years running there were solar eclipses; those who spoke on affairs largely attributed blame to Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Then came three successive years of solar eclipses, and memorialists increasingly blamed Wang Feng.

sentences.zh: 而谷永等遂著之許氏，許氏自知為鳳所不佑。

translations.literal: And Gu Yong and others thereupon fastened it on the Xu clan; the Xu clan knew for themselves that they were not protected by Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yong and his allies pinned the omen on the Xu family, and the Xus understood they had no shelter under Wang Feng.

sentences.zh: 久之，皇后寵亦益衰，而後宮多新愛。

translations.literal: After a long time, the empress's favor also increasingly waned, while the rear palace had many new favorites.
translations.idiomatic: As time passed the empress faded from favor, and fresh rivals multiplied in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 後姊平安剛侯夫人謁等為媚道祝詛後宮有身者王美人及鳳等，事發覺，太后大怒，下吏考問，謁等誅死，許後坐廢處昭台宮，親屬皆歸故郡山陽，後弟子平恩侯旦就國。

translations.literal: The empress's elder sister, Lady Ye the wife of Marquis Ping'an Ganghou, and others practiced 'seductive arts,' praying and cursing against pregnant women of the rear palace including Lady Wang and Feng; when the affair was discovered, the empress dowager was greatly angry; she handed them to officials for interrogation; Ye and the others were executed; Empress Xu was stripped of rank for her involvement and confined to Zhaotai Palace; her kin were all returned to their native commandery Shanyang; her nephew Marquis of Pingen Dan went to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: Her sister Lady Ye, wife of the Marquis of Ping'an Gang, and others had used witchcraft to curse pregnant women in the harem, including Lady Wang and Wang Feng; when it came out, the empress dowager flew into a rage. Official inquiry followed; Ye and her accomplices were put to death; Empress Xu was deposed and sent to Zhaotai Palace; her family was sent home to Shanyang; her nephew Dan, Marquis of Pingen, was ordered to his estate.

sentences.zh: 凡立十四年而廢，在昭台歲餘，還徙長定宮。

translations.literal: In all she had been established fourteen years when she was deposed; she remained at Zhaotai over a year, then was moved again to Changding Palace.
translations.idiomatic: She had been empress fourteen years before her fall; she spent a little over a year at Zhaotai, then was transferred to Changding Palace.

sentences.zh: 後九年，上憐許氏，下詔曰：「蓋聞仁不遺遠，誼不忘親。

translations.literal: Nine years later the sovereign pitied the Xu clan and issued an edict saying: 'We have heard that benevolence does not abandon the distant, and righteousness does not forget kin.'
translations.idiomatic: Nine years afterward the emperor took pity on the Xu family and proclaimed: "They say the humane do not cast off the far-off, and duty does not forsake one's kin."

sentences.zh: 前平安剛侯夫人謁坐大逆罪，家屬幸蒙赦令，歸故郡。

translations.literal: Formerly Lady Ye of Marquis Ping'an Ganghou had committed the crime of great rebellion; her household was fortunately covered by an amnesty edict and returned to their native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ye had been condemned for grave treason, but her people were spared by an amnesty and allowed back to Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 朕惟平恩戴侯，先帝外祖，魂神廢棄，莫奉祭祀，念之未嘗忘於心。

translations.literal: We consider Marquis Dai of Pingen, the former emperor's maternal grandfather—his spirit has been cast aside with none to present sacrifices; thinking of this We have never forgotten it in Our heart.
translations.idiomatic: We remember Marquis Dai of Pingen, our late father's grandfather on his mother's side—his altar stands neglected with no one to tend it, and the thought has never left Us.

sentences.zh: 其還平恩侯旦及親屬在山陽郡者。

translations.literal: Let Marquis of Pingen Dan and his kin who are in Shanyang commandery return.
translations.idiomatic: Let Marquis Dan of Pingen and his relatives dwelling in Shanyang come back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 」是歲，廢後敗。

translations.literal: That year the deposed empress met ruin.
translations.idiomatic: That same year the fallen empress was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 先是，廢後姊靡寡居，與定陵侯淳于長私通，因為之小妻。

translations.literal: Earlier, the deposed empress's elder sister Mi, widowed, had carried on a secret affair with Marquis of Dingling Chunyu Chang and thereby became his lesser wife.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier her sister Mi, a widow, had become Chunyu Chang's concubine after an illicit affair with him.

sentences.zh: 長紿之曰：「我能白東宮，復立許後為左皇后。

translations.literal: Chang deceived her, saying: 'I can speak to the Eastern Palace and restore Empress Xu as left empress.'
translations.idiomatic: Chang lied to her: "I can persuade the empress dowager to reinstate your sister as empress—call her the left empress if you like."

sentences.zh: 」廢後因靡私賂遺長，數通書記相報謝。

translations.literal: The deposed empress thereupon through Mi privately bribed and gifted Chang, repeatedly exchanging letters of reporting and thanks.
translations.idiomatic: The ruined empress sent gifts through Mi and exchanged letter after letter with Chang in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 長書有悖謾，發覺，天子使廷尉孔光持節賜廢後藥，自殺，葬延陵交道廄西。

translations.literal: Chang's letters contained rebellion and deceit; when discovered, the Son of Heaven ordered Commandant of Justice Kong Guang to bear the staff of authority and grant the deposed empress poison; she killed herself and was buried west of the relay stable at the intersection road of Yanling.
translations.idiomatic: His correspondence proved treasonous; once exposed, the emperor sent Kong Guang with an imperial baton to give the deposed empress poison; she took her own life and was interred west of the posting-house crossroads near Yanling.

sentences.zh: 孝成班婕妤

translations.literal: Lady Ban, Favorite Beauty of Emperor Xiaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ban, worthy companion of Emperor Cheng.

sentences.zh: 孝成班婕妤。

translations.literal: Lady Ban, Favorite Beauty of Emperor Xiaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ban, companion of Emperor Cheng.

sentences.zh: 帝初即位選入後宮。

translations.literal: When the emperor first ascended the throne she was selected and entered the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: She entered the harem as soon as Cheng took the throne.

sentences.zh: 始為少使，蛾而大幸，為婕妤，居增成捨，再就館，有男，數月失之。

translations.literal: At first she was a junior attendant; she became beautiful and received great favor; she became a Favorite Beauty and dwelt in the Zengcheng lodge; twice she went to the lying-in quarters; she had a boy and lost him after several months.
translations.idiomatic: She began as a junior maid, then bloomed into favor and was raised to Favorite Beauty, with quarters in Zengcheng. Twice she entered the birthing residence; each time she bore a son who died within months.

sentences.zh: 成帝游於後庭，嘗欲與婕妤同輦載，婕妤辭曰：「觀古圖畫，賢聖之君皆有名臣在側，三代末主乃有嬖女，今欲同輦，得無近似之乎？

translations.literal: When Emperor Cheng roamed the rear palace, he once wished to ride in the same palanquin with the Favorite Beauty; she declined, saying: 'Looking at ancient paintings, sage and worthy lords all had famous ministers at their side; only the last rulers of the three dynasties had favored women. Now wishing to share a palanquin—perhaps would it not approximate that?'
translations.idiomatic: Once when Cheng was strolling the inner gardens he asked Lady Ban to share his carriage; she refused. "In every worthy king's portrait," she said, "wise ministers stand at his side; only the degenerate last rulers of the three ages rode with their mistresses. If we rode together now, would we not resemble them?"

sentences.zh: 」上善其言而止。

translations.literal: The sovereign deemed her words good and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved her argument and dropped the idea.

sentences.zh: 太后聞之，喜曰：「古有樊姬，今有班婕妤。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager heard it, she joyfully said: 'In antiquity there was Fan Ji; now there is Lady Ban the Favorite Beauty.'
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was delighted. "History gave us Fan Ji," she said; "our age has Lady Ban."

sentences.zh: 」婕妤誦《詩》及《竊窕》、《德象》、《女師》之篇。

translations.literal: The Favorite Beauty recited the Odes and the pieces 'Graceful and Pure,' 'Virtue's Image,' and 'Mistress to Women.'
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ban was versed in the Classic of Poetry and the didactic texts on womanly conduct.

sentences.zh: 每進見上疏，依則古禮。

translations.literal: Whenever she advanced to audience or submitted a memorial, she accorded with ancient rites as her rule.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever she appeared before the throne or sent up a memorial, she framed herself by classical precedent.

sentences.zh: 自鴻嘉後，上稍隆於內寵。

translations.literal: From Hongjia onward, the sovereign gradually elevated inner favorites.
translations.idiomatic: After the Hongjia era (20–17 BCE) the emperor began to shower favor on women of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 婕妤進侍者李平，平得幸，立為婕妤。

translations.literal: The Favorite Beauty presented her attendant Li Ping; Ping received favor and was established as Favorite Beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ban introduced her maid Li Ping, who so pleased the emperor that he raised her to the same rank of Favorite Beauty.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「始衛皇后亦從微起。

translations.literal: The sovereign said: 'At the beginning Empress Wei also rose from lowliness.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remarked, "Empress Wei herself began as a lowborn girl."

sentences.zh: 」乃賜平姓曰衛，所謂衛婕妤也。

translations.literal: Thereupon he bestowed on Ping the surname Wei—this is the one called Lady Wei the Favorite Beauty.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore granted Li Ping the surname Wei, and she became known as Lady Wei the Favorite Beauty.

sentences.zh: 其後，趙飛燕姊弟亦從自微賤興，逾越禮制，浸盛於前。

translations.literal: Afterward Zhao Feiyan and her younger sister too rose from utter lowliness, transgressed ritual regulation, and gradually flourished beyond those before.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhao Feiyan and her sister climbed from the gutter as well, shattered every protocol, and soon eclipsed all who had gone before.

sentences.zh: 班婕妤及許皇后皆失寵，稀復進見。

translations.literal: Lady Ban the Favorite Beauty and Empress Xu both lost favor and rarely advanced again to audience.
translations.idiomatic: Both Lady Ban and Empress Xu fell from grace and were seldom admitted to the emperor's presence.

sentences.zh: 鴻嘉三年，趙飛燕譖告許皇后、班婕妤挾媚道，祝詛後宮，詈及主上。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongjia, Zhao Feiyan slanderously reported that Empress Xu and Lady Ban the Favorite Beauty employed seductive arts, prayed and cursed the rear palace, and reviled even the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongjia 3 (18 BCE) Zhao Feiyan accused Empress Xu and Lady Ban of witchcraft—of cursing the harem and even the emperor himself.

sentences.zh: 許皇后坐廢。

translations.literal: Empress Xu was deposed for her involvement.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xu was stripped of her rank.

sentences.zh: 孝問班婕妤，婕妤對曰：「妾聞『死生有命，富貴在天。

translations.literal: The sovereign questioned Lady Ban the Favorite Beauty; she replied: 'Your servant has heard, "Death and life have their allotment; wealth and honor are from Heaven."'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned Lady Ban, who answered: "I have always been taught that life and death are fated, and station comes from Heaven."

sentences.zh: 』修正尚未蒙福，為邪欲以何望？

translations.literal: Correcting oneself and yet not receiving blessing—practicing wickedness, what hope is there?'
translations.idiomatic: A virtuous life may still win no reward—what could witchcraft possibly gain me?'

sentences.zh: 使鬼神有知，不受不臣之訴；

translations.literal: Supposing the ghosts and spirits have knowledge, they do not accept the appeals of the disloyal subject;
translations.idiomatic: If spirits are conscious, they spurn the prayers of traitors;

sentences.zh: 如其無知，訴之何益？

translations.literal: if they have no knowledge, what benefit in appealing to them?
translations.idiomatic: if they are not, what good could prayer do?

sentences.zh: 故不為也。

translations.literal: Therefore your servant would not do it.'
translations.idiomatic: So I would never stoop to such things.'

sentences.zh: 」上善其對，憐憫之，賜黃金百斤。

translations.literal: The sovereign deemed her reply good, pitied her, and granted one hundred jin of yellow gold.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted her defense, pitied her, and gave her a hundred jin of gold.

sentences.zh: 趙氏姊弟驕妒，婕妤恐久見危，求供養太后長信宮，上許焉。

translations.literal: The Zhao sisters were arrogant and jealous; the Favorite Beauty feared that over time she would meet peril; she requested to supply support to the empress dowager at Changxin Palace; the sovereign granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao sisters were proud and spiteful; Lady Ban feared for her life if she stayed and asked to withdraw to wait upon the empress dowager in Changxin Palace. The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 婕妤退處東宮，作賦自傷悼，其辭曰：

translations.literal: The Favorite Beauty retired to dwell in the Eastern Palace and composed a rhapsody to wound and mourn herself; its words say:
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ban withdrew to the Eastern Palace and wrote a lament in fu form; it begins:

sentences.zh: 承祖考之遺德兮，何性命之淑靈，登薄軀於宮闕兮，充下陳於後庭。

translations.literal: Receiving the bequeathed virtue of grandfathers and fathers—oh, how good and numinous is this life! I ascended my slight body to the palace gates; I filled the lower ranks of the rear court.
translations.idiomatic: I entered the palace blessed by my ancestors' goodness; though my frame is slight I was chosen to walk these halls and take my place among the women who serve below the throne.

sentences.zh: 蒙聖皇之渥惠兮，當日月之盛明，揚光烈之翕赫兮，奉隆寵於增成。

translations.literal: Covering with the rich favor of the sage sovereign—facing the blazing brightness of sun and moon; displaying dazzling splendor—I received towering favor in Zengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The holy emperor showered me with grace; I basked in radiance like sun and moon and burned bright with favor in the lodge at Zengcheng.

sentences.zh: 既過幸於非位兮，竊庶幾乎嘉時，每寤寐而累息兮，申佩離以自思，陳女圖以鏡監兮，顧女史而問詩。

translations.literal: Having passed beyond fortune in a station not my due—secretly hoping for a fine season; every waking and sleeping I sigh in layers; I straighten sash and ornaments and reflect on myself; I spread the women's charts for mirror-surveillance; I turn to the female scribe and ask of the Odes.
translations.idiomatic: Favored beyond my station, I still hoped for happy days; night and day I sighed, straightened my sash, and examined myself against the painted models of virtue, turning to the court instructress and the Classic of Poetry.

sentences.zh: 悲晨婦之作戒兮，哀褒、閻之為郵；

translations.literal: I grieve how wicked consorts became warnings to posterity; I mourn Bao and Yan as bearers of blame;
translations.idiomatic: I tremble at the warnings drawn from evil favorites and mourn how Bao Si and others carried ruin to their kings;

sentences.zh: 美皇、英之女虞兮，榮任、姒之母周。

translations.literal: I praise Ehuang and Nüying who gave daughters to Shun; I honor Jiang Yuan and Si who mothered Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: I praise Ehuang and Nüying who wed Shun, and Jiang Yuan and Taisi who mothered the house of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 雖愚陋其靡及兮，敢捨心而忘茲？

translations.literal: Though stupid and lowly I do not reach them—dare I cast aside my heart and forget this?
translations.idiomatic: Coarse and dull though I am beside such women, how could I lay duty aside or forget their warning?

sentences.zh: 歷年歲而悼懼兮，閔蕃華之不滋。

translations.literal: Year after year passing I mourn and fear; I pity that luxuriant blossom does not flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Years slip by in dread; the lush bloom I hoped for never ripens.

sentences.zh: 痛陽祿與柘館兮，仍襁褓而離災，豈妾人之殃咎兮？

translations.literal: I ache for Yanglu and Zhe Lodge—still in swaddling bands yet parted by disaster; is it your servant-woman's baleful guilt?
translations.idiomatic: I mourn the sons born at Yanglu and Zhe Lodge—babes still in the cradle, torn away by fate; is this my own curse?

sentences.zh: 將天命之不可求。

translations.literal: Or is Heaven's mandate not to be sought?
translations.idiomatic: Or is Heaven's decree simply beyond our plea?

sentences.zh: 白日忽已移光兮，遂暗莫而昧幽，猶被覆載之厚德兮，不廢捐於罪郵。

translations.literal: The bright sun suddenly has shifted its radiance; then endless darkness and gloom close in; still covered by the thick virtue that bears and carries me—not cast aside for crimes transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: Daylight suddenly fled and left me in shadow; still Heaven's kindness that wraps the world has not cast me off for my faults.

sentences.zh: 奉供養於東宮兮，托長信之末流，供灑掃於帷幄兮，永終死以為期。

translations.literal: Offering support at the Eastern Palace; entrusting myself to the lowest current of Changxin; supplying sprinkling and sweeping within curtains and canopies—taking death to the end as my term.
translations.idiomatic: I serve the Eastern Palace and cling to the humblest duty at Changxin; I will sweep the dust behind the curtains until my life ends.

sentences.zh: 願歸骨於山足兮，依松柏之餘休。

translations.literal: I wish to return my bones to the mountain's foot; to rely on the lingering shade of pines and cypresses.
translations.idiomatic: Let my bones rest at the mountain's foot beneath pines and cypress that shade the dead.

sentences.zh: 重曰：「潛玄官兮幽以清，應門閉兮禁闥ECE7。

translations.literal: Again it says: 'Hidden in the dark palace—deep and clear; the outer gate is shut—the forbidden inner portals…'
translations.idiomatic: The refrain runs: "Deep in the dark palace, hushed and chill; the outer doors stand shut and the inner wards are barred."

sentences.zh: 華殿塵兮玉階，中庭萋兮綠草生。

translations.literal: Splendid halls dust-covered—the jade steps; in the central courtyard luxuriant—green grass grows.
translations.idiomatic: Moted halls and jade stairways; the courtyard runs wild with green grass.

sentences.zh: 廣室陰兮帷幄暗，房櫳虛兮風泠泠。

translations.literal: Spacious chambers shadowed—curtains and canopies dark; window lattices empty—wind cold and clear.
translations.idiomatic: Vast rooms lie in shadow, curtains drawn tight; empty casements admit only a thin cold wind.

sentences.zh: 感帷裳兮發紅羅，紛綷絲G-*3祭兮紈素聲。

translations.literal: Stirred by curtain-skirts—unfurling red gauze; tangled rustling silks—the sound of fine white silk.
translations.idiomatic: Scarlet gauze stirs at my sleeve; white silk whispers as it brushes and sighs.

sentences.zh: 神眇眇兮密靚處，君不御兮誰為榮？

translations.literal: Spirit distant-distant—in secret quiet dwelling; if the lord does not ride—who is honored?
translations.idiomatic: My spirit wanders this lonely chamber; if my lord never visits, what glory can there be?

sentences.zh: 俯視兮丹墀，思君兮履綦。

translations.literal: Looking down—the cinnabar courtyard; thinking of the lord—the tread of his patterned shoes.
translations.idiomatic: I gaze down the vermilion steps and trace in dust the prints his shoes once left.

sentences.zh: 仰視兮雲屋，雙涕兮橫流。

translations.literal: Looking up—the cloud-patterned roof; paired tears—flow athwart.
translations.idiomatic: I lift my eyes to the painted rafters and tears stream unchecked down both cheeks.

sentences.zh: 顧左右兮和顏，酌羽觴兮銷憂。

translations.literal: Glancing left and right—with harmonious countenance; pouring the feather-cup wine—dispelling sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: I force a calm face for those beside me and lift the winged cup to drown my grief.

sentences.zh: 惟人生兮一世，忽一過兮若浮。

translations.literal: Only human life—one generation; suddenly once passed—like floating.
translations.idiomatic: We are granted one human span; it flashes past like foam on the stream.

sentences.zh: 已獨享兮高明，處生民兮極休。

translations.literal: Already alone enjoying—height and brightness; dwelling among the living people—utmost repose.
translations.idiomatic: Once I alone dwelt in these lofty halls and stood among mortals at the summit of joy.

sentences.zh: 勉虞精兮極樂，與福祿兮無期。

translations.literal: Striving for mindful essence—utmost joy; together with blessing and emolument—without end.
translations.idiomatic: I strove to sustain pure devotion and endless bliss—or so I dreamed fortune might endure.

sentences.zh: 《綠衣》兮《白華》，自古兮有之。

translations.literal: 'Green Collar'—'White Blossoms'—from antiquity there have been such.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes knew 'Green Robe' and 'White Flowers'—such sorrow is older than memory.

sentences.zh: 至成帝崩，婕妤充奉園陵，薨，因葬園中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Cheng died, the Favorite Beauty served fully at the garden tumulus; she passed away and was accordingly buried within the park.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng died Lady Ban took charge of offerings at his tomb park; she died there and was buried within its grounds.

sentences.zh: 孝成趙皇后

translations.literal: Empress Zhao of Emperor Xiaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhao of Emperor Cheng.

sentences.zh: 孝成趙皇后，本長安宮人。

translations.literal: Empress Zhao of Emperor Xiaocheng was originally a palace woman of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhao began life as a servant girl in the Chang'an palaces.

sentences.zh: 初生時，父母不舉，三日不死，乃收養之。

translations.literal: At first birth, her parents did not rear her; three days she did not die, then they took her in and raised her.
translations.idiomatic: Her parents tried to expose her at birth; when she lived three days they relented and kept her.

sentences.zh: 及壯，屬陽阿主家，學歌舞，號曰飛燕。

translations.literal: When grown, she belonged to the household of Mistress Yang'e; she studied songs and dances and was titled Flying Swallow.
translations.idiomatic: As a woman grown she entered the troupe of Mistress Yang'e, trained in song and dance, and took the stage name Flying Swallow.

sentences.zh: 成帝嘗微行出。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng once went out incognito.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng once slipped from the palace in disguise.

sentences.zh: 過陽阿主，作樂，上見飛燕而說之，召入宮，大幸。

translations.literal: Passing Mistress Yang'e, music was performed; the sovereign saw Flying Swallow and delighted in her; he summoned her into the palace and greatly favored her.
translations.idiomatic: He stopped at Mistress Yang'e's house during a performance, fell under Flying Swallow's spell, brought her to the palace, and cherished her above all others.

sentences.zh: 有女弟復召入，俱為婕妤，貴傾後宮。

translations.literal: Having a younger sister, she too was summoned in; both became Favorite Beauties; their nobility overturned the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: Her younger sister followed her in; both became Favorite Beauties and together dominated the harem.

sentences.zh: 許後之廢也，上欲立趙婕妤。

translations.literal: When Empress Xu was deposed, the sovereign wished to establish Lady Zhao the Favorite Beauty.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Xu fell, the emperor meant to raise Lady Zhao to empress.

sentences.zh: 皇太后嫌其所出微甚，難之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager resented that her origins were extremely low and found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager despised her humble birth and resisted.

sentences.zh: 太后姊子淳于長為侍中，數往來傳語，得太后指，上立封趙婕妤父臨為成陽侯。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's elder sister's son Chunyu Chang was gentleman attendant at the palace gates; he repeatedly went back and forth conveying words; obtaining the empress dowager's intent, the sovereign immediately enfeoffed Lady Zhao the Favorite Beauty's father Lin as Marquis of Chengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Her nephew Chunyu Chang, a palace attendant, shuttled messages until he secured the dowager's tacit consent; the emperor then ennobled Zhao Lin, Flying Swallow's father, as Marquis of Chengyang.

sentences.zh: 後月餘，乃立婕妤為皇后。

translations.literal: After more than a month, he then established the Favorite Beauty as empress.
translations.idiomatic: A month later Lady Zhao was proclaimed empress.

sentences.zh: 追以長前白罷昌陵功，封為定陵侯。

translations.literal: Retroactively, because Chang had earlier reported and stopped the Chang mausoleum project, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingling.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyu Chang was rewarded retroactively—with a marquisate at Dingling—for having talked the emperor out of the wasteful Changling project.

sentences.zh: 皇后既立，後寬少衰，而弟絕幸，為昭儀。

translations.literal: Once the empress was established, favor toward her slightly waned, while her younger sister received ultimate favor and became Brilliant Companion.
translations.idiomatic: After her enthronement the elder Zhao cooled slightly while her sister became Brilliant Companion and monopolized the emperor's love.

sentences.zh: 居昭陽捨，其中庭彤硃，而殿上髹漆，切皆銅沓黃金塗，白玉階，壁帶往往為黃金釭，函藍田璧，明珠、翠羽飾之，自後宮未嘗有焉。

translations.literal: She dwelt in the Zhaoyang lodge; its central courtyard was cinnabar red, while the hall above was lacquered; every joint was copper casing gold-coated; white jade steps; wall bands often had yellow gold rings inset with Lantian jade disks, decorated with bright pearls and kingfisher feathers—such had never been in the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: She lived in Zhaoyang Hall: vermilion courtyard, lacquered rafters, gilt bronze fittings, white jade stairs, wall rings of hammered gold holding disks of Lantian jade, studded with pearls and kingfisher plumes—splendor unknown to any earlier consort.

sentences.zh: 姊弟顓寵十餘年，卒皆無子。

translations.literal: The sisters monopolized favor over ten years; in the end both had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: For more than a decade the sisters owned the emperor's heart, yet neither bore him an heir.

sentences.zh: 末年，定陶王來朝，王祖母傅太后私賂遺趙皇后、昭儀，定陶王竟為太子。

translations.literal: In the last years, the Prince of Dingtao came to court; the prince's grandmother Grand Empress Dowager Fu privately bribed and gifted Empress Zhao and the Brilliant Companion; the Prince of Dingtao in the end became heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the reign the Prince of Dingtao visited the capital; his grandmother Lady Fu secretly bought off Empress Zhao and her sister so that the prince was named heir.

sentences.zh: 明年春，成帝崩。

translations.literal: The next spring, Emperor Cheng died.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring Emperor Cheng died.

sentences.zh: 帝素強，無疾病。

translations.literal: The emperor had always been strong; he had no illness.
translations.idiomatic: He had always been vigorous and showed no sign of sickness.

sentences.zh: 是時，楚思王衍、梁王立來朝，明旦當辭去，上宿供張白虎殿。

translations.literal: At this time Prince Sima Yan of Chu and Prince Sima Li of Liang had come to court; the next dawn they were to take leave and depart; the sovereign lodged with provisions spread at White Tiger Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The kings of Chu and Liang were in the capital to bid farewell the next morning; Cheng spent the night at White Tiger Hall, where quarters had been prepared.

sentences.zh: 又欲拜左將軍孔光為丞相，已刻侯印書贊。

translations.literal: He also wished to appoint Left General Kong Guang as chancellor; the marquis seal had already been carved and the commendation written.
translations.idiomatic: He planned to promote Kong Guang to chancellor that night—the seal was cut and the patent of enfeoffment drafted.

sentences.zh: 昏夜平善，鄉晨，傅褲襪欲起，因失衣，不能言，晝漏上十刻而崩。

translations.literal: At dusk and night all was peaceful; toward dawn, having put on trousers and socks he wished to rise; because he dropped his robe he could not speak; by the clepsydra's tenth mark of day he died.
translations.idiomatic: He seemed well at bedtime; near dawn, after pulling on his hose and reaching for his robe, he collapsed dumbstruck; before the morning clock had run ten marks he was dead.

sentences.zh: 民間歸罪趙昭儀，皇太后詔大司馬莽、丞相大司空曰：「皇帝暴崩，群眾言雚嘩怪之。

translations.literal: Common folk attributed guilt to Zhao the Brilliant Companion; the empress dowager issued an edict to Grand Marshal Mang, Chancellor, and Grand Minister of Works, saying: 'The emperor died suddenly; the crowd's words are clamorous and wonder at it.'
translations.idiomatic: The people blamed Zhao the Brilliant Companion; the empress dowager summoned Wang Mang, the chancellor, and the minister of works and declared, "The emperor has died without warning, and rumor runs wild."

sentences.zh: 掖庭令輔等在後庭左右，侍燕迫近，雜與御史、丞相、廷尉治問皇帝起居發病狀。

translations.literal: Let Commissioner of the Lateral Courts Fu and others who waited left and right in the rear palace, attending banquets in close attendance, join with the imperial clerk, chancellor, and commandant of justice to investigate and question the circumstances of the emperor's daily life and the onset of illness.'
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Fu and others who waited on the emperor's revels shall assist the censor, chancellor, and chief judge in tracing his final hours and how the sickness began.'

sentences.zh: 」趙昭儀自殺。

translations.literal: Zhao the Brilliant Companion killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao the Brilliant Companion took her own life.

sentences.zh: 哀帝既立，尊趙皇后為皇太后，封太后弟侍中駙馬都尉欽為新成侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ai had been established, he honored Empress Zhao as empress dowager and enfeoffed the empress dowager's younger brother, gentleman attendant and chief commandant of attendants Qin, as Marquis of Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ai raised Empress Zhao to empress dowager and made her brother Qin—who served as attendant and chief of the mounted escort—Marquis of Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 趙氏侯者凡二人。

translations.literal: Those of the Zhao clan who were marquises numbered two in all.
translations.idiomatic: Two members of the Zhao clan held marquisates.

sentences.zh: 後數月，司隸解光奏言：

translations.literal: Several months later Metropolitan Commander Xie Guang submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Months afterward Metropolitan Commander Xie Guang memorialized:

sentences.zh: 臣聞許美人及故中宮史曹宮皆御幸孝成皇帝，產子，子隱不見。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that Lady Xu the Fair and former palace clerk of the central palace Cao Gong both received imperial favor from Emperor Xiaocheng and bore sons; the sons were hidden and have not appeared.
translations.idiomatic: I have learned that Lady Xu and the former palace clerk Cao Gong both lay with Emperor Cheng and gave birth—yet those infants vanished without trace.

sentences.zh: 臣遣從事掾業、史望驗問知狀者掖庭獄丞籍武，故中黃門王舜、吳恭、靳嚴，官婢曹曉、道房、張棄，故趙昭儀御者於客子、王偏、臧兼等，皆曰宮即曉子女，前屬中宮，為學事史，通《詩》，授皇后。

translations.literal: Your servant dispatched adjutants Ye and Shi Wang to examine and question those who knew the circumstances: assistant jailer of the rear palace Ji Wu, former yellow-gate internuncios Wang Shun, Wu Gong, and Jin Yan, palace slave-girls Cao Xiao, Daofang, and Zhang Qi, former attendants for Zhao the Brilliant Companion Yu Kezi, Wang Pian, Zang Jian, and others—all said Gong was Xiao's daughter; formerly she belonged to the central palace, was clerk for academic affairs, understood the Odes, and instructed the empress.
translations.idiomatic: I sent clerks Ye and Shi Wang to question jailer Ji Wu, eunuchs Wang Shun, Wu Gong, and Jin Yan, maids Cao Xiao, Daofang, and Zhang Qi, and the Brilliant Companion's grooms Yu Kezi, Wang Pian, and Zang Jian. All testified that Cao Gong was Cao Xiao's daughter, once a tutor-scribe in the empress's bureau who taught the Odes to the empress.

sentences.zh: 房與宮對食，元延元年中宮語房曰：「陛下幸宮。

translations.literal: Fang and Gong took meals as paired attendants; in the first year of Yuanyan the central palace spoke to Fang, saying: 'The sovereign has favored Gong.'
translations.idiomatic: Daofang and Gong had paired as 'table partners.' In Yuanyan 1 (12 BCE) the empress told Daofang, "The emperor has favored Gong."

sentences.zh: 」後數月，曉入殿中，見宮腹大，問宮。

translations.literal: Several months later, Xiao entered the hall and saw Gong's belly large; she asked Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Months later Cao Xiao entered the hall, saw Gong's swollen belly, and demanded an explanation.

sentences.zh: 宮曰：「御幸有身。

translations.literal: Gong said: 'Imperial favor—there is pregnancy.'
translations.idiomatic: Gong answered, "His Majesty's attentions have left me with child."

sentences.zh: 」其十月中，宮乳掖庭牛官令捨，有婢六人，中黃門田客持詔記，盛綠綈方底，封御史中丞印，予武曰：「取牛官令捨婦人新產兒，婢六人，盡置暴室獄，毋問兒男女，誰兒也！

translations.literal: In that tenth month Gong gave milk at the cattle-keeper director's lodge of the rear palace; there were six slave-girls; yellow-gate attendant Tian Ke bore an edict-note contained in a green silk square-bottom case sealed with the assistant imperial clerk's seal, and gave it to Wu, saying: 'Take the woman who has newly delivered at the cattle-keeper director's lodge, her newborn child, and the six slave-girls; put them all in Exposure Chamber prison; do not ask whether the baby is male or female or whose child it is!'
translations.idiomatic: That tenth month Gong bore her child in the rear-palace cattle-keeper's quarters with six maids in attendance. The eunuch Tian Ke arrived with an edict slip in a green silk pouch sealed with the deputy censor's stamp and told Ji Wu: "Round up the new mother, the infant, and all six girls; lock them in the Exposure Chamber jail—and don't ask whether the baby is a boy or a girl or who fathered it."

sentences.zh: 」武迎置獄，宮曰：「善臧我兒胞，丞知是何等兒也！

translations.literal: Wu received them and placed them in prison; Gong said: 'Well hide my child's afterbirth—the assistant knows what sort of child this is!'
translations.idiomatic: Wu locked them away; Gong cried, "Guard my baby's caul—the jailer already knows what bloodline this is!"

sentences.zh: 」後三日，客持詔記與武，問：「兒死未？

translations.literal: Three days later Ke brought an edict-note to Wu and asked: 'Is the child dead yet?'
translations.idiomatic: Three days later Tian Ke returned with another slip: "Is the baby dead yet?"

sentences.zh: 手書對牘背。

translations.literal: Write the reply by hand on the back of the slip.
translations.idiomatic: He was to answer in his own hand on the reverse of the document.

sentences.zh: 」武即書對：「兒見在，未死。

translations.literal: Wu immediately wrote in reply: 'The child is present; not dead.'
translations.idiomatic: Wu wrote back at once: "The child still lives."

sentences.zh: 」有頃，客出曰：「上與昭儀大怒，奈何不殺？

translations.literal: After a moment Ke came out and said: 'The sovereign and the Brilliant Companion are greatly angry—why have you not killed him?'
translations.idiomatic: Soon Tian Ke emerged furious: "The emperor and the Brilliant Companion are beside themselves—why is that child still breathing?"

sentences.zh: 」武叩頭啼曰：「不殺兒，自知當死；

translations.literal: Wu knocked his head and wept, saying: 'If I do not kill the child, I know I ought to die;
translations.idiomatic: Wu kowtowed, weeping: "Spare the baby and I know I die;

sentences.zh: 殺之，亦死！

translations.literal: kill him—I die as well!'
translations.idiomatic: murder him—and I die all the same!"

sentences.zh: 」即因客奏封事，曰：「陛下未有繼嗣，子無貴賤，唯留意！

translations.literal: Thereupon through Ke he submitted a sealed memorial, saying: 'Your Majesty has not yet an heir; a son has no rank high or low—only attend to this!'
translations.idiomatic: He sent in a sealed plea through Tian Ke: "You still have no successor; no infant should be discarded for birth alone—think on it, Majesty!"

sentences.zh: 」奏入，客復持詔記予武曰：「今夜漏上五刻，持兒與舜，會東交掖門。

translations.literal: When the memorial went in, Ke again bore an edict-note to Wu, saying: 'Tonight at the fifth mark on the clepsydra, bring the child to Shun and meet at the east intersecting lateral gate.'
translations.idiomatic: When it had been read, Tian Ke brought fresh orders: "At the fifth night-watch bring the child to Wang Shun at the east junction of the lateral gates."

sentences.zh: 」武因問客：「陛下得武書，意何如？

translations.literal: Wu thereupon asked Ke: 'When His Majesty received Wu's writing, what was his mood?'
translations.idiomatic: Wu asked Tian Ke how the emperor had taken his memorial.

sentences.zh: 」曰：「瞠也。

translations.literal: He said: 'He stared blankly.'
translations.idiomatic: "He only stared," was the reply.

sentences.zh: 」武以兒付舜。

translations.literal: Wu handed the child to Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Wu surrendered the infant to Wang Shun.

sentences.zh: 舜受詔，內兒殿中，為擇乳母，告「善養兒，且有賞。

translations.literal: Shun received the edict, brought the child inside the hall, chose a wet nurse for him, and instructed: 'Nurse the child well—there will be reward.
translations.idiomatic: Shun carried the baby into the palace, chose a wet nurse, and told her, "Care for him faithfully—you will be rewarded.

sentences.zh: 毋令漏洩！

translations.literal: Do not let it leak!'
translations.idiomatic: Tell no one."

sentences.zh: 」舜擇棄為乳母，時兒生八九日。

translations.literal: Shun chose Qi as wet nurse; at the time the child was eight or nine days old.
translations.idiomatic: He picked the maid Qi as nurse when the boy was barely nine days old.

sentences.zh: 後三日，客復持詔記，封如前予武，中有封小綠篋，記曰：「告武以篋中物書予獄中婦人，武自臨飲之。

translations.literal: Three days later Ke again bore an edict-note, sealed as before, and gave it to Wu; inside was a sealed small green box; the note said: 'Tell Wu to give to the woman in prison what is written with the objects in the box; Wu shall personally oversee her drinking it.'
translations.idiomatic: Three days later Tian Ke delivered another sealed packet. Inside lay a small green casket with orders for Ji Wu to pass its contents to the prisoner and watch her swallow them himself.

sentences.zh: 」武發篋中有裹藥二枚，赫蹄書，曰：「告偉能：努力飲此藥，不可復入。

translations.literal: Wu opened the box: inside were two wrapped doses of medicine and writing on thin tissue paper, saying: 'Tell Weineng: strive to drink this medicine; do not enter again.
translations.idiomatic: Wu opened it to find two doses of poison on tissue-thin paper: "Tell Weineng to swallow this willingly and never return.

sentences.zh: 女自知之！

translations.literal: You yourself know it!'
translations.idiomatic: You know why."

sentences.zh: 」偉能即宮。

translations.literal: Weineng is Gong.'
translations.idiomatic: "Weineng" was Cao Gong's informal name.

sentences.zh: 宮讀書已，曰：「果也，欲姊弟擅天下！

translations.literal: When Gong had finished reading the writing, she said: 'As expected—they wish the sisters to monopolize the realm!'
translations.idiomatic: After reading she cried, "Just as I thought—the Zhao sisters mean to own the empire between them!

sentences.zh: 我兒男也，額上有壯發，類孝元皇帝。

translations.literal: My child is male; on his forehead he has strong hair—like Emperor Xiaoyuan.'
translations.idiomatic: My son is a boy with the royal swirl on his brow—he resembles Emperor Yuan."

sentences.zh: 今兒安在？

translations.literal: Where is the child now?'
translations.idiomatic: Where is he now?

sentences.zh: 危殺之矣！

translations.literal: He has been perilously killed!'
translations.idiomatic: They have murdered him!"

sentences.zh: 奈何令長信得聞之？

translations.literal: How could you let Changxin hear of it?'
translations.idiomatic: How could you let word reach Changxin Palace?"

sentences.zh: 宮飲藥死。

translations.literal: Gong drank the medicine and died.
translations.idiomatic: Gong drank the poison and died.

sentences.zh: 後宮婢六人召入，出語武曰：「昭儀言『女無過。

translations.literal: The six rear-palace slave-girls were summoned in; coming out they spoke to Wu, saying: 'The Brilliant Companion says, "You women have no fault.
translations.idiomatic: The six maids were summoned inside and emerged to tell Wu: "The Brilliant Companion says you committed no crime.

sentences.zh: 寧自殺邪，若外家也？

translations.literal: Better kill yourselves—or like the empress's kin?"'
translations.idiomatic: Will you die by your own hands, or shall your kin die for you?"

sentences.zh: 』我曹言願自殺。

translations.literal: We said we wished to kill ourselves.'
translations.idiomatic: We answered that we preferred to take our own lives."

sentences.zh: 」即自繆死。

translations.literal: Thereupon they strangled themselves.
translations.idiomatic: They hanged themselves at once.

sentences.zh: 武皆表奏狀。

translations.literal: Wu memorialized all of it in tabular form.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Wu laid the whole affair before the throne in formal memorials.

sentences.zh: 棄所養兒十一日，宮長李南以詔書取兒去，不知所置。

translations.literal: On the eleventh day of Qi's nursing the child, palace chief Li Nan took the child away by imperial edict; it was not known where he was placed.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven days after Qi began nursing the baby, Director Li Nan carried him off under sealed orders; no one learned what became of him.

sentences.zh: 許美人前在上林涿沐館，數召入飾室中若捨，一歲再三召，留數月或半歲御幸。

translations.literal: Lady Xu the Fair had formerly been at Zhuomu Lodge in Shanglin; she was several times summoned into the ornament chamber's dwellings; within one year she was summoned three times again; she stayed several months or half a year and received imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xu had quarters at Zhuomu Lodge in the Shanglin Park; the emperor repeatedly brought her to his dressing chambers—sometimes two or three summons in a single year—and kept her for months at a stretch.

sentences.zh: 元延二年懷子，其十一月乳。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanyan she conceived; in its eleventh month she gave milk.
translations.idiomatic: She conceived in Yuanyan 2 (11 BCE) and delivered that winter.

sentences.zh: 詔使嚴持乳醫及五種和藥丸三，送美人所。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yan to bring the wet-nurse physician and three pills of the five-ingredient compound medicine and deliver them to the Fair One's place.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered his attendant Yan to bring the obstetrician and three doses of a five-ingredient restorative to Lady Xu's lodge.

sentences.zh: 後客子、偏、兼聞昭儀謂成帝曰：「常給我言從中宮來，即從中宮來，許美人兒何從生中？

translations.literal: Later Kezi, Pian, and Jian heard the Brilliant Companion say to Emperor Cheng: 'You constantly tell me that when you come from the central palace you truly come from the central palace—how then could Lady Xu the Fair's child have been born from the central palace?
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kezi, Wang Pian, and Zang Jian overheard the Brilliant Companion rebuke Cheng: "You always swear you come straight from the empress—so how could Lady Xu's baby have been gotten there?

sentences.zh: 許氏竟當復立邪！

translations.literal: Is the Xu clan after all to be restored!'
translations.idiomatic: Are we to watch the Xu clan rise again?"

sentences.zh: 」懟，以手自搗，以頭擊壁戶柱，從床上自投地，啼泣不肯食，曰：「今當安置我，欲歸耳！

translations.literal: Enraged, she struck with her hands, beat her head against wall, door, and pillar, threw herself from the couch to the ground, wept and refused to eat, saying: 'Now you must settle me—I wish to go home!'
translations.idiomatic: She flew into a rage, hammered her own breast, dashed her head against posts and walls, rolled from the couch wailing, and refused food: "Dispose of me as you please—I want to leave this place!"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「今故告之，反怒為！

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Now I purposely told you—and you turn angry!'
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said, "I confided in you honestly—why this tantrum?"

sentences.zh: 殊不可曉也。

translations.literal: Utterly incomprehensible.'
translations.idiomatic: It makes no sense at all."

sentences.zh: 」帝亦不食。

translations.literal: The emperor also did not eat.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stopped eating as well.

sentences.zh: 昭儀曰：「陛下自知是，不食為何？

translations.literal: The Brilliant Companion said: 'Your Majesty knows yourself that this is so—why not eat?'
translations.idiomatic: She asked, "If your conscience is clear, why starve yourself?"

sentences.zh: 陛下常自言『約不負女』，今美人有子，竟負約，謂何？

translations.literal: Your Majesty constantly said yourself, "In covenant I will not betray you"—now the Fair One has a son; you have after all betrayed the covenant—what of it?'
translations.idiomatic: You swore you would never break faith with me—yet Lady Xu has borne a son. What do you call that but betrayal?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「約以趙氏，故不立許氏。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'The covenant was for the Zhao clan—therefore We did not establish the Xu clan.'
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Our pact was for the house of Zhao—that is why Empress Xu fell."

sentences.zh: 使天下無出趙氏上者，毋憂也！

translations.literal: Let there be none in the realm above the Zhao clan—have no worry!'
translations.idiomatic: So long as no rival rises above your Zhao kin, you have nothing to fear."

sentences.zh: 」後詔使嚴持綠囊書予許美人，告嚴曰：「美人當有以予女，受來，置飾室中簾南。

translations.literal: Afterward an edict ordered Yan to bear a green-sachet letter to Lady Xu the Fair, instructing Yan: 'The Fair One will have something to give you—receive it and place it south of the curtain in the ornament chamber.'
translations.idiomatic: Later Cheng sent Yan to Lady Xu with a letter in a green silk pouch, telling him, "She will hand you something—bring it back and leave it south of the curtain in the dressing hall."

sentences.zh: 」美人以葦篋一合盛所生兒，緘封，及綠囊報書予嚴。

translations.literal: The Fair One placed the newborn child in a reed box of one measure, sealed it shut, together with the green-sachet reply letter gave them to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xu packed her newborn in a reed basket, sealed it, and gave Yan the reply that matched the green pouch.

sentences.zh: 嚴持篋書，置飾室簾南去。

translations.literal: Yan bore the box and letter, placed them south of the curtain in the ornament chamber, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Yan set the basket and letter where he had been told and withdrew.
