sentences.zh: 帝與昭儀坐，使客子解篋緘。

translations.literal: The emperor sat with the Brilliant Companion and ordered Kezi to open the box seals.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng and the Brilliant Companion sat together while Yu Kezi broke the seals.

sentences.zh: 未已，帝使客子、偏、兼皆出，自閉戶，獨與昭儀在。

translations.literal: Before it was finished, the emperor ordered Kezi, Pian, and Jian all to go out; he himself closed the door and was alone with the Brilliant Companion.
translations.idiomatic: Before they could finish, Cheng sent the attendants away, bolted the door, and remained alone with her.

sentences.zh: 須臾開戶，呼客子、偏、兼，使緘封篋及綠綈方底，推置屏風東。

translations.literal: After a moment he opened the door, called Kezi, Pian, and Jian, ordered them to seal shut the box and the green silk square-bottom case, and push them east of the screen.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later he opened the door, called the three men back, had them reseal the basket and green pouch, and slide both behind the eastern screen.

sentences.zh: 恭受詔，持篋方底予武，皆封以御史中丞印，曰：「告武：篋中有死兒，埋屏處，勿令人知。

translations.literal: Gong received the edict, bore the box and square-bottom case to Wu, both sealed with the assistant imperial clerk's seal, saying: 'Tell Wu: inside the box is a dead child—bury it where the screen is; do not let others know.'
translations.idiomatic: Wu Gong took imperial orders, delivered the sealed bundle to Ji Wu with the deputy censor's stamp, and said, "There is a dead infant inside—bury it behind that screen and breathe no word of it."

sentences.zh: 」武穿獄樓垣下為坎，埋其中。

translations.literal: Wu dug a pit beneath the jail tower wall and buried it therein.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Wu dug a trench under the prison wall and interred the child there.

sentences.zh: 故長定許貴人及故成都、平阿侯家婢王業、任孋、公孫習前免為庶人，詔召入，屬昭儀為私婢。

translations.literal: Former Worthy Lady Xu of Changding and former slave-girls Wang Ye, Ren Li, and Gongsun Xi of the households of Marquis of Chengdu and Marquis of Ping'e had earlier been dismissed to commoner status; an edict summoned them in and assigned them to the Brilliant Companion as private slave-girls.
translations.idiomatic: Xu the Fair of Changding and three maids—Wang Ye, Ren Li, and Gongsun Xi—from the Chengdu and Ping'e households, lately stripped of rank, were recalled and handed over as the Brilliant Companion's personal servants.

sentences.zh: 成帝崩，未幸梓宮，倉卒悲哀之時，昭儀自知罪惡大，知業等故許氏、王氏婢，恐事洩，而以大婢羊子等賜予業等各且十人，以尉其意，屬「無道我家過失。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Cheng died, before he had been laid in the catalpa coffin, in the haste of grief the Brilliant Companion knew herself guilty of great crimes; knowing that Ye and the others had formerly been Xu and Wang slave-girls, she feared the affair would leak; therefore she bestowed on Ye and each of the others roughly ten senior slave-girls such as Yangzi to soothe their feelings, instructing: 'Do not speak of misdeeds in my household.'
translations.idiomatic: While Cheng's body still awaited the catafalque, the Brilliant Companion knew how grave her sins were. Ye and the others had served the Xu and Wang clans and might talk; she quieted them by gifting each ten senior maids like Yangzi and whispered, "Never breathe a word about what happened in my house."

sentences.zh: 元延二年五月，故掖庭令吾丘遵謂武曰：「掖庭丞吏以下皆與昭儀合通，無可與語者，獨欲與武有所言。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Yuanyan, former commissioner of the lateral courts Wuqiu Zun said to Wu: 'Assistant commissioners and clerks of the lateral courts and below all collude with the Brilliant Companion; there is none with whom to speak—I alone wish to say something to Wu.'
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanyan 2 (11 BCE), the retired lateral-court chief Wuqiu Zun told Ji Wu, "Every underling in this bureau is in the Brilliant Companion's pocket; you are the only man I dare trust."

sentences.zh: 我無子，武有子，是家輕族人，得無不敢乎？

translations.literal: I have no sons; Wu has sons—this household lightly regards clan kin—could it be they dare not?
translations.idiomatic: I am childless while you have heirs—doesn't this court treat its own kin too lightly for anyone to speak up?"

sentences.zh: 掖庭中御幸生子者輒死，又飲藥傷墮者無數，欲與武共言之大臣，票騎將軍貪耆錢，不足計事，奈何令長信得聞之？

translations.literal: In the lateral courts those who bore children after imperial favor died immediately; moreover those who drank medicine and were injured or miscarried were countless; I wished to speak together with Wu to the great ministers—but the general of agile cavalry is greedy for money and not worth planning affairs with—how could Changxin be allowed to hear of it?'
translations.idiomatic: Every woman here who bore the emperor's child has died; countless others were poisoned into miscarriage. I meant to approach the high ministers with you—but the general of agile cavalry cares only for silver and cannot be trusted. How could word ever reach Changxin Palace?"

sentences.zh: 」遵後病困，謂武：「今我已死，前所語事，武不能獨為也，慎語！」

translations.literal: Later Zun fell gravely ill and said to Wu: 'Now I am about to die; the matters spoken of before—Wu cannot act alone on them—be careful in speaking!'
translations.idiomatic: When Zun lay dying he warned Ji Wu, "I am leaving you what we discussed—you cannot carry it alone. Guard your tongue."

sentences.zh: 皆在今年四月丙辰赦令前。

translations.literal: All were before the amnesty edict of bingchen in the fourth month of this year.
translations.idiomatic: Every crime predated the general amnesty proclaimed on bingchen in the fourth month of this year.

sentences.zh: 臣謹案永光三年男子忠等發長陵傅夫人塚。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully cites: in the third year of Yongguang the men Zhong and others opened the tomb of Lady Fu at Changling.
translations.idiomatic: Consider Yongguang 3 (41 BCE), when grave robbers broke into Lady Fu's tomb at Changling.

sentences.zh: 事更大赦，孝元皇帝下詔曰：「此朕不當所得赦也。

translations.literal: The affair encountered a great amnesty; Emperor Xiaoyuan issued an edict saying: 'This is not what We ought to have received amnesty for.'
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty would have spared them, yet Emperor Yuan ruled, "This outrage falls outside any pardon I may grant."

sentences.zh: 」窮治，盡伏辜，天下以為當。

translations.literal: They were pursued to the limit; all submitted guilt; the realm deemed it fitting.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a full prosecution; every culprit confessed; the empire agreed justice had been done.

sentences.zh: 魯嚴公夫人殺世子，齊桓召而誅焉，《春秋》予之。

translations.literal: The wife of Duke Yan of Lu killed the heir apparent; Duke Huan of Qi summoned and executed her—the Spring and Autumn approves it.
translations.idiomatic: When Duchess Zhuang of Lu murdered her heir, Duke Huan of Qi had her executed—and the Spring and Autumn praises him for it.

sentences.zh: 趙昭儀傾亂聖朝，親滅繼嗣，家屬當伏天誅。

translations.literal: Zhao the Brilliant Companion overturned and threw into confusion the sage court; personally she extinguished heirs—her household ought to suffer Heaven's execution.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao the Brilliant Companion wrecked the dynasty and murdered its heirs; her clan merits Heaven's own sentence.

sentences.zh: 前平安剛侯夫人謁坐大逆，同產當坐，以蒙赦令，歸故郡。

translations.literal: Formerly Lady Ye of Marquis Ping'an Ganghou sat guilty of great rebellion; those born of the same womb ought to sit guilt; because they received cover of an amnesty edict, they returned to their native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ye's treason should have doomed her whole bloodline, yet an amnesty sent them home to Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 今昭儀所犯尤悖逆，罪重於謁，而同產親屬皆在尊貴之位，迫近幃幄，群下寒心，非所以懲惡崇誼示四方也。

translations.literal: Now the Brilliant Companion's offenses are especially rebellious; her guilt is heavier than Ye's—yet siblings and kin all occupy honored positions, pressing close to bed-curtains; those below are chilled at heart—this is not the means to punish evil, elevate righteousness, and show the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The Brilliant Companion's crimes dwarf Lady Ye's, yet her kin still crowd the inner chambers and wear noble rank—the court trembles and the empire sees no justice.

sentences.zh: 請事窮竟，丞相以下議正法。

translations.literal: Your servant requests the affair be pursued to the end; let chancellor and below deliberate correct punishment.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the case be prosecuted to its conclusion and that the chancellor and his colleagues determine the proper penalty.

sentences.zh: 哀帝於是免新成侯趙欽、欽兄子成陽侯訢，皆為庶人，將家屬徙遼西郡。

translations.literal: Emperor Ai thereupon dismissed Marquis of Xincheng Zhao Qin and Qin's elder brother's son Marquis of Chengyang Xin; both became commoners; their households were moved to Liaoxi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ai stripped Zhao Qin and his nephew Xin—Marquises of Xincheng and Chengyang—of rank and banished their families to Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 時議郎耿育上疏言：

translations.literal: At the time Consultant Geng Yu submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Then Consultant Geng Yu delivered this memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞繼嗣失統，廢適立庶，聖人法禁，古今至戒。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that when succession loses proper thread and the heir apparent is cast aside to establish a lesser son, the sages forbid it by law—it is the utmost warning of past and present.
translations.idiomatic: Disordering the succession—deposing the heir for a younger son—is barred by every sage and cited as the gravest warning in history.

sentences.zh: 然大怕見歷知適，逡循固讓，委身吳粵，權變所設，不計常法，致位王季，以崇聖嗣，卒有天下，子孫承業，七八百載，功冠三王，道德最備，是以尊號追及大王。

translations.literal: Yet Taibo of Zhou understood that the legitimate heir must rule; yielding his claim, he withdrew to Wu and Yue—a deliberate breach of ordinary law to secure the dynasty—elevated Wang Ji to preserve the sacred succession, and won the realm for eight hundred years, surpassing the Three Dynasties in merit and virtue, so posterity honored even King Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Taibo of Zhou knew he must yield to the rightful heir; he withdrew to Wu and Yue, bent ritual for the realm's sake, and elevated his brother Jili so the sacred line could rule. His house held All-under-Heaven for seven or eight hundred years, outshining the three dynasties in virtue—posterity even hailed his father as King Tai.

sentences.zh: 故世必有非常之變，然後乃有非常之謀。

translations.literal: Therefore the age must have extraordinary transformation; only afterward may there be extraordinary planning.
translations.idiomatic: Extraordinary times demand extraordinary measures—that is the lesson of the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 孝成皇帝自知繼嗣不以時立，念雖末有皇子，萬歲之後未能持國，權柄之重，制於女主，女主驕盛則耆欲無極，少主幼弱則大臣不使，世無周公抱負之輔，恐危社稷，傾亂天下。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaocheng knew himself that succession was not established in due season; pondering that although ultimately there was no imperial son, after ten thousand years he could not sustain the state—the weight of power-holders would be controlled by the mistress of women; if the mistress of women was arrogant and flourishing then greedy desires would know no limit; if the young lord was young and weak then great ministers would not serve; if in the age there were none like the Zhou dukes who embraced him as regent—he feared endangering altars of soil and grain and overturning chaos under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng understood he had named no heir in good time. Without a son of his own body the dynasty would totter after his death; power would fall to an empress dowager—and an arrogant dowager knows no limit, while an infant emperor leaves ministers unteachable. With no Zhou-style regent in sight, the altars could fall and the realm descend into chaos.

sentences.zh: 知陛下有賢聖通明之德，仁孝子愛之恩，懷獨見之明，內斷於身，故廢後宮就館之漸，絕微嗣禍亂之根，乃欲致位陛下以安宗廟。

translations.literal: Knowing that Your Majesty possesses worthy sage lucid virtue, benevolent filial son-loving grace, cherishing insight alone clear within, deciding within yourself—therefore cutting off the gradual growth of rear palace lying-in lodges, severing the root of slender-heir calamity and chaos—thereupon wishing to convey position to Your Majesty to settle the ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: He saw in you lucid virtue, filial devotion, and independence of mind; he broke off every rear-palace pregnancy that might breed turmoil and chose you to steady the ancestral shrines.

sentences.zh: 愚臣既不能深援安危，定金匱之計，又不知推演聖德，述先帝之志，乃反覆校省內，暴露私燕，誣污先帝傾惑之過，成結寵妾妒媚之誅，甚失賢聖遠見之明，逆負先帝憂國之意。

translations.literal: Your foolish servant was neither able deeply to cite safety and peril and settle the metal coffer plan, nor knew to unfold sage virtue and narrate the former emperor's intent—instead repeatedly examining the inner palace, exposing private banquet intimacies, slandering and defiling the former emperor's overturning delusion fault, completing and tying up favored concubines' jealous flattery executions—greatly losing worthy sage far-seeing lucidity, opposing and betraying the former emperor's intent of worrying for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Petty officials could neither shore up the succession nor expound your father's purpose; instead they raked the women's quarters, aired imperial pillow-talk, smeared late Emperor Cheng as besotted, and branded his favorites for jealousy—all of which insults his foresight and betrays the care he took for the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 夫論大德不拘俗，立大功不合眾，此乃孝成皇帝至思所以萬萬於眾臣，陛下聖德盛茂所以符合於皇天也，豈當世庸庸斗筲之臣所能及哉！

translations.literal: Now discussing great virtue does not bind to vulgar custom; establishing great merit does not accord with the multitude—this is Emperor Xiaocheng's utmost reflection whereby he exceeded myriad times the mass of ministers; Your Majesty's sage virtue flourishes lushly whereby it accords with august Heaven—how could the commonplace petty-measure ministers of the present age reach it!
translations.idiomatic: Great virtue ignores vulgar opinion; great deeds never please every petty voice—that was Cheng's surpassing wisdom and is your own Heaven-matching excellence—far beyond the grasp of narrow clerk-minds.

sentences.zh: 且褒廣將順君父之美，匡救銷滅既往之過，古今通義也。

translations.literal: Moreover praising and amplifying what follows and complies with lord father's excellence; correcting rescue and erasing prior faults—is the universal righteousness of past and present.
translations.idiomatic: It is universal duty to magnify a father's virtues and quietly mend his faults.

sentences.zh: 事不當時固爭，防禍於未然，各隨指阿從，以求容媚，晏駕之後，尊號已定，萬事已訖，乃探追不及之事，訐揚幽昧之過，此臣所深痛也！

translations.literal: When affairs were not timely they ought firmly to have contested; preventing calamity before it happened—each following fingerings and flattering compliance to seek accommodating flattery; after the carriage at dusk, honored titles already fixed, myriad affairs already concluded—then probing things beyond recall, exposing and spreading hidden obscure faults—this is what your servant deeply grieves!
translations.idiomatic: Men who said nothing when disaster could have been forestalled now fawn for favor; once the late emperor's catafalque had passed and his temple name was fixed, they rake up stale gossip and whisper of bedroom sins—that makes honest ministers sick.

sentences.zh: 願下有司議，即如臣言，宜宣佈天下，使鹹嘵知先帝聖意所起。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes it be handed down to offices for deliberation; if just as your servant has spoken, it ought be proclaimed throughout the realm, causing all to understand clearly whence arose the former emperor's sage intent.
translations.idiomatic: Refer this to the ministries; if my reading holds, proclaim it so the empire understands why late Emperor Cheng acted as he did.

sentences.zh: 不然，空使謗議上及山陵，下流後世，遠聞百蠻，近布海內，甚非先帝托後之意也。

translations.literal: If not, vainly causing slander and debate to reach upward to the mound tombs and flow downward to later generations, heard afar by the hundred Man and spread near within the seas—greatly this is not the former emperor's intent in entrusting posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise slander will cling to his tomb, stain later ages, and reach every barbarian ear—nothing could betray his trust in you more cruelly.

sentences.zh: 蓋孝子善述父之志，善成人之事，唯陛下省察！

translations.literal: For the filial son is good at narrating father's intent and good at completing father's affairs—I beg Your Majesty to examine!
translations.idiomatic: A true son completes his father's work and guards his memory—I beg you weigh this carefully.

sentences.zh: 哀帝為太子，亦頗得趙太后力，遂不竟其事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ai was heir apparent, he also rather received Empress Dowager Zhao's force; thereupon the affair was not carried through.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ai owed his nomination largely to Empress Dowager Zhao, so the prosecution stalled.

sentences.zh: 傅太后恩趙太后，趙太后亦歸心，故成帝母及王氏皆怨之。

translations.literal: Grand Empress Dowager Fu favored Empress Dowager Zhao; Empress Dowager Zhao also turned heart—therefore Emperor Cheng's mother and the Wang clan all resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Fu courted Lady Zhao and won her loyalty; Cheng's mother and the Wang family bitterly resented the bargain.

sentences.zh: 哀帝崩，王莽白太后詔有司曰：「前皇太后與昭儀俱侍帷幄，姊弟專寵錮寢，執賊亂之謀，殘滅繼嗣以危宗廟，悖天犯祖，無為天下母之義。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ai died, Wang Mang reported to the empress dowager and ordered the offices: 'The former empress dowager and the Brilliant Companion together attended curtains and canopies; elder sister and younger sister monopolized favor and confined the bedchamber; they held murderous rebellious plots; they slaughtered and extinguished heirs to endanger ancestral temples; they rebelled against Heaven and offended ancestors—they have no righteousness to be mothers under Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: After Ai died Wang Mang persuaded Grand Empress Dowager Wang to proclaim: "The former empress dowager and Zhao the Brilliant Companion shared the inner chambers; the sisters locked Cheng in their embrace and schemed murder; they destroyed heirs and threatened the temples—they offended Heaven and the ancestors and forfeited any claim to be mothers of the realm."

sentences.zh: 貶皇太后為孝成皇後，徙居北宮。

translations.literal: Demote the empress dowager to Empress of Emperor Xiaocheng; move her to dwell in Northern Palace.'
translations.idiomatic: Strip her of empress dowager rank, style her merely Empress of Cheng, and remove her to the Northern Palace."

sentences.zh: 」後月餘，復下詔曰：「皇后自知罪惡深大，朝請希闊，失婦道，無共養之禮，而有狼虎之毒，宗室所怨，海內之仇也，而尚在小君之位，誠非皇天之心。

translations.literal: More than a month later, another edict was issued: 'The empress knows herself guilty of deep enormity; court audiences are sparse and distant; she has lost the way of a wife; she has no ritual of joint nourishment—yet has wolf-and-tiger poison; she is what the imperial lineage resents and what within the seas hates—yet still occupies the petty lord's position—truly this is not august Heaven's intent.'
translations.idiomatic: A month later another edict charged that Zhao knew her guilt yet spurned ritual attendance on her mother-in-law, behaved not as a wife but as a wolf, earned the hatred of the imperial clan and the whole empire—and could no longer pretend to Heaven's favor.

sentences.zh: 夫小不忍亂大謀，恩之所不能已者義之所割也。

translations.literal: When small things are not endured, great plans are thrown into chaos; what kindness cannot stop is what righteousness must cut away.'
translations.idiomatic: Mercy that poisons great designs must yield to justice that severs even kinship."

sentences.zh: 今廢皇后為庶人，就其園。

translations.literal: Now depose the empress as commoner; let her go to her garden estate.'
translations.idiomatic: She is hereby reduced to commoner rank and confined to her tomb park."

sentences.zh: 」是日自殺。

translations.literal: That day she killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: That same day she took her own life.

sentences.zh: 立十六年而誅。

translations.literal: Having been established sixteen years, she was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen years after her enthronement she perished under sentence.

sentences.zh: 先是，有童謠曰：「燕燕，尾□□，張公子，時相見。

translations.literal: Earlier there had been a children's rhyme: 'Swallow swallow, tail … Lord Zhang's son, meeting from time to time.'
translations.idiomatic: A children's song had run: "Swallow, swallow, tail held high—Lord Zhang's heir meets her again and again"—two graphs were missing in the text.

sentences.zh: 木門倉琅根，燕飛來，啄皇孫。

translations.literal: Wooden gate, granary ring-root—swallow flies in, pecks imperial grandson.
translations.idiomatic: "Through the wooden gate with its bronze rings the swallow darts to peck the imperial grandson."

sentences.zh: 皇孫死，燕啄矢。

translations.literal: Imperial grandson dies—swallow pecks arrow.
translations.idiomatic: "When the grandson dies the swallow picks at the shaft."

sentences.zh: 」成帝每微行出，常與張放俱，而稱富平侯家，故曰張公子。

translations.literal: Whenever Emperor Cheng went out incognito, he constantly was together with Zhang Fang and called it the Marquis of Fuping's household—therefore 'Lord Zhang's son.'
translations.idiomatic: Cheng used to sneak out with Zhang Fang of the Fuping marquisate—the "Lord Zhang" of the rhyme.

sentences.zh: 倉琅根，宮門銅鍰也。

translations.literal: 'Granary ring-root'—the palace gate's bronze rings.
translations.idiomatic: "Bronze rings" meant the metal fittings on palace gates.

sentences.zh: 孝元傅昭儀

translations.literal: Fu the Brilliant Companion of Emperor Xiaoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Fu, Brilliant Companion of Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 孝元傅昭儀，哀帝祖母也。

translations.literal: Fu the Brilliant Companion of Emperor Xiaoyuan was Emperor Ai's grandmother.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Fu the Brilliant Companion was Emperor Ai's grandmother.

sentences.zh: 父河內溫人，蚤卒，母更嫁為魏郡鄭翁妻，生男惲。

translations.literal: Her father was a man of Wen in Henei; he died early; her mother remarried as wife of Old Zheng of Wei commandery and bore a son Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Her father was a commoner of Wen in Henei who died young; her mother remarried an old man named Zheng in Wei commandery and bore a son, Fu Yun.

sentences.zh: 昭儀少為上官太后才人，自元帝為太子，得進幸。

translations.literal: The Brilliant Companion in youth was a talented lady for Empress Dowager Shangguan; from when Yuan was heir apparent, she obtained advancement and favor.
translations.idiomatic: She entered service as a talented lady under Grand Empress Dowager Shangguan and won Yuan's favor while he was still heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 元帝即位，立為婕妤，甚有寵。

translations.literal: When Yuan ascended the throne, she was established as Favorite Beauty and was greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan took the throne she became Favorite Beauty and basked in his favor.

sentences.zh: 為人有材略，善事人，下至宮人左右，飲酒酹地，皆祝延之。

translations.literal: In conduct she had talent and stratagem; she was skilled at serving people—down to palace attendants left and right; when drinking she poured libations on the ground—all prayed for her long life.
translations.idiomatic: She was clever and winning; she cultivated everyone from the emperor down to the meanest maid, and when servants poured libations for her they prayed she would live forever.

sentences.zh: 產一男一女，女為平都公主，男為定陶恭王。

translations.literal: She bore one son and one daughter; the daughter became Princess Pingdu, the son King Gong of Dingtao.
translations.idiomatic: She bore a daughter, Princess Pingdu, and a son who became the king of Dingtao posthumously styled Gong.

sentences.zh: 恭王有材藝，尤愛於上。

translations.literal: King Gong had talent and arts; he was especially loved by the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: The boy showed gifts that endeared him above all others to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 元帝既重傅婕妤，及馮婕妤亦幸，生中山孝王，上欲殊之於後宮，以二人皆有子為王，上尚在，未得稱太后，乃更號曰昭儀，賜以印綬，在婕妤上。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan having esteemed Lady Fu the Favorite Beauty, when Lady Feng the Favorite Beauty also received favor and bore King Xiao of Zhongshan, the sovereign wished to distinguish them in the rear palace; because both had sons who were kings while the sovereign still lived and could not be styled empress dowager—therefore he changed their title to Brilliant Companion, bestowed seals and ribbons on them, ranking them above Favorite Beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan favored Lady Fu and later Lady Feng, who bore the king of Zhongshan; wishing to honor both mothers while he still lived—when neither could yet be called empress dowager—he invented the title Brilliant Companion, complete with seals of office, ranking them above ordinary Favorite Beauties.

sentences.zh: 昭其儀，尊之也。

translations.literal: Making manifest her ritual display—that is honoring her.
translations.idiomatic: The title proclaimed their heightened ceremonial standing.

sentences.zh: 至成、哀時，趙昭儀、董昭儀皆無子，猶稱焉。

translations.literal: Down to the times of Cheng and Ai, Zhao the Brilliant Companion and Dong the Brilliant Companion both had no sons—yet still were so titled.
translations.idiomatic: Under Cheng and Ai, Zhao and Dong held the same title though neither bore an heir.

sentences.zh: 元帝崩，傅昭儀隨王歸國，稱定陶太后。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan died, Fu the Brilliant Companion followed the king to his kingdom and was titled Grand Empress Dowager of Dingtao.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan died Lady Fu accompanied her son to Dingtao and was honored as that kingdom's grand empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 後十年，恭王薨，子代為王。

translations.literal: Ten years later King Gong died; his son succeeded as king.
translations.idiomatic: A decade later King Gong died and his son inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 王母曰丁姬。

translations.literal: The king's mother was Lady Ding.
translations.idiomatic: The new king's mother was Lady Ding.

sentences.zh: 傅太后躬自養視，既壯大，成帝無繼嗣。

translations.literal: Grand Empress Dowager Fu personally reared and watched over him; once he had grown to maturity, Emperor Cheng had no successor.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Empress Dowager Fu had raised the boy herself; by the time he came of age Cheng still had no heir.

sentences.zh: 時中山孝王在。

translations.literal: At that time King Xiao of Zhongshan was alive.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Zhongshan was still living.

sentences.zh: 元延四年，孝王及定陶王皆入朝。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanyan, King Xiao and the King of Dingtao both entered court.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanyan 4 both the Zhongshan and Dingtao princes arrived for audience.

sentences.zh: 傅太后多以珍寶賂遺趙昭儀及帝舅票騎將軍王根，陰為王求漢嗣。

translations.literal: Grand Empress Dowager Fu largely used treasures to bribe and gift Zhao the Brilliant Companion and the emperor's maternal uncle, General of Agile Cavalry Wang Gen; secretly she sought the Han succession for the king.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Fu showered Zhao the Brilliant Companion and Wang Gen with jewels, quietly bidding them make her grandson heir to the throne.

sentences.zh: 昭儀及根皆見上無子，欲豫自結為久長計，更稱譽定陶王。

translations.literal: The Brilliant Companion and Gen both saw that the sovereign had no sons; they wished to bind themselves early for a long-term plan; they further praised the King of Dingtao.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Cheng childless, Zhao and Wang curried lasting favor by praising the Dingtao prince.

sentences.zh: 上亦自器之，明年，遂征定陶王立為太子，語在《哀紀》。

translations.literal: The sovereign also himself esteemed him; the next year he then summoned the King of Dingtao and established him as heir apparent—the account is in the 'Annals of Ai.'
translations.idiomatic: Cheng admired the youth himself; the following year he summoned him as crown prince—the full story is told in the annals of Emperor Ai.

sentences.zh: 月餘，天子立楚孝王孫景為定陶王，奉恭王后。

translations.literal: After more than a month the Son of Heaven established Jing, grandson of King Xiao of Chu, as King of Dingtao to serve King Gong's posterity.
translations.idiomatic: A month later another prince was installed at Dingtao to maintain King Gong's line.

sentences.zh: 太子議欲謝，少傅閻崇以為：「《春秋》不以父命廢王父命，為人後之禮不得顧私親，不當謝。

translations.literal: The heir apparent deliberated wishing to give thanks; Junior Tutor Yan Chong held: 'The Spring and Autumn does not use father's command to dismiss grandfather's command; the ritual of being another's heir does not permit regard for private kin—he ought not give thanks.'
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince debated whether to thank Dingtao for releasing him; Yan Chong cited the Spring and Autumn: an heir may not put birth parents before his adoptive line—thanks were improper.

sentences.zh: 」太傅趙玄以為當謝，太子從之。

translations.literal: Senior Tutor Zhao Xuan held that he ought to give thanks; the heir apparent followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Senior Tutor Zhao Xuan disagreed, and the prince sided with him.

sentences.zh: 詔問所以謝狀，尚書劾奏玄，左遷少府，以光祿勳師丹為太傅。

translations.literal: An edict asked the reason for the thanks; the imperial secretary impeached and memorialized Xuan; he was demoted to minister of the lesser treasury; Superintendent of the Imperial Household Shi Dan was made senior tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When the court demanded his reasons, Zhao Xuan was impeached, demoted to oversee the lesser treasury, and replaced as senior tutor by Shi Dan.

sentences.zh: 詔傅太后與太子母丁姬自居定陶國邸，下有司議皇太子得與傅太后、丁姬相見不，有司秦議不得相見。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Grand Empress Dowager Fu and the heir apparent's mother Lady Ding to dwell themselves at the Dingtao kingdom lodge in the capital; it ordered subordinates to deliberate whether the imperial heir might meet Grand Empress Dowager Fu and Lady Ding or not; subordinates memorialized deliberation that they could not meet.
translations.idiomatic: Fu and Lady Ding were lodged at the Dingtao hostel while officials debated visits; the memorialists ruled that mother and grandmother must not see the heir.

sentences.zh: 頃之，成帝母王太后欲令傅太后、丁姬十日一至太子家，成帝曰：「太子丞正統，當共養陛下，不得復顧私親。

translations.literal: Shortly, Emperor Cheng's mother Grand Empress Dowager Wang wished to order Grand Empress Dowager Fu and Lady Ding once every ten days to go to the heir apparent's house; Emperor Cheng said: 'The heir apparent inherits the legitimate line; he ought jointly to nourish Your Majesty—he cannot again regard private kin.'
translations.idiomatic: Grand Empress Dowager Wang proposed fortnightly visits; Cheng refused: "The crown prince belongs to the imperial line now—his duty is to you, not his birth kin."

sentences.zh: 」王太后曰：「太子小，而傅太后抱養之。

translations.literal: Grand Empress Dowager Wang said: 'The heir apparent is small, and Grand Empress Dowager Fu embraced and reared him.'
translations.idiomatic: She answered, "The boy is young; Lady Fu nursed him as a grandmother would."

sentences.zh: 今至太子家，以乳母恩耳，不足有所妨。

translations.literal: Now going to the heir apparent's house is only wet-nurse kindness—it is not enough to cause hindrance.'
translations.idiomatic: Let her visit as a foster mother would—where is the harm in that?"

sentences.zh: 」於是令傅太后得至太子家。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered that Grand Empress Dowager Fu could reach the heir apparent's house.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng relented and allowed Lady Fu to call on the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 丁姬以不安養太子，獨不得。

translations.literal: Lady Ding because she had not peacefully reared the heir apparent alone did not obtain permission.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ding, who had not raised him, was denied the same privilege.

sentences.zh: 成帝崩，哀帝即位。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng died; Emperor Ai ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng died Ai succeeded.

sentences.zh: 王太后詔令傅太后、丁姬十日一至未央宮。

translations.literal: Grand Empress Dowager Wang issued an edict ordering Grand Empress Dowager Fu and Lady Ding once every ten days to come to Weiyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Empress Dowager Wang allowed Fu and Lady Ding to visit Weiyang Palace every ten days.

sentences.zh: 高昌侯董宏希指，上書言宜立丁姬為帝太后。

translations.literal: Marquis of Gaochang Dong Hong hoped to hit the mark; he submitted a memorial saying Ding Ji ought to be established as empress dowager of the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Hong of Gaochang curried favor by urging that Lady Ding be named empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 師丹劾奏：「宏懷邪誤朝，不道。

translations.literal: Shi Dan impeached and memorialized: 'Hong harbors wickedness and misleads the court—non-canonical.'
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dan impeached Hong for sedition against proper government.

sentences.zh: 」上初即位，謙讓，從師丹言止。

translations.literal: The sovereign had recently ascended the throne; deferring, he followed Shi Dan's words and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The new emperor, still cautious, accepted Shi's advice and dropped the proposal.

sentences.zh: 後乃白令王太后下詔，尊定陶恭王為恭皇。

translations.literal: Afterward he reported and ordered Grand Empress Dowager Wang to issue an edict honoring King Gong of Dingtao as Gong Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Later he persuaded Grand Empress Dowager Wang to canonize his late father as Emperor Gong.

sentences.zh: 哀帝因是曰：「《春秋》『母以子貴』，尊傅太后為恭皇太后，丁姬為恭皇后，各置左右詹事，食邑如長信宮、中宮。

translations.literal: Emperor Ai thereupon said: 'The Spring and Autumn says "the mother is honored through the son"'—honor Grand Empress Dowager Fu as Gong Grand Empress Dowager, Ding Ji as Gong Empress; for each establish left and right household stewards; food fiefs as Changxin Palace and Central Palace.'
translations.idiomatic: Ai cited the Spring and Autumn—"a mother rises with her son"—and titled Fu Gong grand empress dowager and Ding Gong empress, each with household stewards and incomes matching the principal palaces.

sentences.zh: 追尊恭皇太后父為崇祖侯，恭皇后父為褒德侯。

translations.literal: Retroactively honor Gong Grand Empress Dowager's father as Marquis of Chongzu, Gong Empress's father as Marquis of Baode.'
translations.idiomatic: Their fathers were posthumously ennobled as Marquises of Chongzu and Baode.

sentences.zh: 」後歲餘，遂下詔曰：「漢家之制，推親親以顯尊尊，定陶恭皇之號不宜復稱定陶。

translations.literal: More than a year later an edict was issued: 'Han institutions extend kin-loving to manifest honor-of-honors; the title Gong Emperor of Dingtao ought not again be called Dingtao.'
translations.idiomatic: A year later an edict declared that Han ritual distinguished degrees of kin—the canonized ruler must shed the old regional title "Dingtao."

sentences.zh: 其尊恭皇太后為帝太太后，丁后為帝太后。

translations.literal: Honor Gong Grand Empress Dowager as Empress Dowager Supreme of the Emperor; Ding as Empress Dowager of the Emperor.'
translations.idiomatic: Fu became "Empress Dowager Supreme" and Ding plain "Empress Dowager of the Emperor."

sentences.zh: 」後又更號帝太太后為皇太太后，稱永信宮，帝太后稱中安宮，而成帝母太皇太后本稱長信宮，成帝趙后為皇太后，並四太后，各置少府、太僕，秩皆中二千石。

translations.literal: Later again the title Empress Dowager Supreme of the Emperor was changed to Grand Empress Dowager Supreme; she was called Yongxin Palace; Empress Dowager of the Emperor was called Zhong'an Palace; while Emperor Cheng's mother Grand Empress Dowager was originally called Changxin Palace; Empress Zhao of Cheng was empress dowager—together four empress dowagers; each had established minister of the lesser treasury and grand coachman; rank all fully two thousand shi at middle grade.'
translations.idiomatic: Fu was renamed grand empress dowager supreme with residence Yongxin; Ding took Zhong'an; Cheng's mother kept Changxin; Zhao Feiyan remained empress dowager—four dowagers at once, each with her own minister of the lesser treasury and grand coachman at two thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 為恭皇立寢廟於京師，比宣帝父悼皇考制度，序昭穆於前殿。

translations.literal: For Gong Emperor they established resting temple in the capital, comparable to Emperor Xuan's father's posthumous Emperor Dao system; they ordered zhao-mu generations in the front hall.
translations.idiomatic: A metropolitan shrine was built for Emperor Gong on the model of Emperor Xuan's father, with proper father-son placement in the imperial temple.

sentences.zh: 傅太后父同產弟四人，曰子孟、中叔、子元、幼君。

translations.literal: Grand Empress Dowager Fu's father's uterine younger brothers were four, named Zimeng, Zhongshu, Ziyuan, and Youjun.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Fu's father had four full brothers: Zimeng, Zhongshu, Ziyuan, and Youjun.

sentences.zh: 子孟子喜至大司馬，封高武侯。

translations.literal: Zimeng's son Xi rose to grand marshal and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Gaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Zimeng's son Xi became grand marshal and Marquis of Gaowu.

sentences.zh: 中叔子晏亦大司馬，封孔鄉侯。

translations.literal: Zhongshu's son Yan likewise was grand marshal and enfeoffed as Marquis of Kongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshu's son Yan also rose to grand marshal with the marquisate of Kongxiang.

sentences.zh: 幼君子商封汝昌侯，為太后父崇祖侯後，更號崇祖曰汝昌哀侯。

translations.literal: Youjun's son Shang was enfeoffed Marquis of Ruchang; he succeeded Grand Empress Dowager's father Marquis of Chongzu; Chongzu's title was changed to Marquis Ai of Ruchang.
translations.idiomatic: Youjun's son Shang held Ruchang and inherited Lady Fu's father's line, whose tomb title became Marquis Ai of Ruchang.

sentences.zh: 太后同母弟鄭惲前死，以惲子業為陽信侯，追尊惲為陽信節侯。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's uterine younger brother Zheng Yun had died earlier; Yun's son Ye was made Marquis of Yangxin; Yun was retroactively honored Marquis Jie of Yangxin.
translations.idiomatic: Her half-brother Zheng Yun was dead; his son Ye became Marquis of Yangxin and Yun was honored posthumously as Marquis Jie.

sentences.zh: 鄭氏、傅氏侯者凡六人，大司馬二人，九卿二千石六人，侍中諸曹十餘人。

translations.literal: Those of the Zheng and Fu clans who were marquises numbered six in all; grand marshals two; nine ministers and two-thousand-shi officials six; gentlemen-in-waiting and bureau heads over ten.
translations.idiomatic: The Zheng and Fu houses held six marquisates, two grand marshals, six ministerial posts, and more than a dozen palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 傅太后既尊，後尤驕，與成帝母語，至謂之嫗。

translations.literal: Once Grand Empress Dowager Fu was honored, she became especially arrogant; speaking with Emperor Cheng's mother she went so far as to call her 'old woman.'
translations.idiomatic: Elevated to supremacy, Lady Fu grew insolent enough to call Cheng's mother an old hag.

sentences.zh: 與中山孝王母馮太后並事元帝，追怨之，陷以祝詛罪，令自殺。

translations.literal: She together with King Xiao of Zhongshan's mother Grand Empress Dowager Feng had both served Emperor Yuan; nursing old resentment, she trapped her with a curse-crime and ordered her to kill herself.
translations.idiomatic: She had shared Yuan's harem with Lady Feng of Zhongshan; nursing old grudges she framed her for witchcraft and drove her to suicide.

sentences.zh: 元壽元年崩，合葬渭陵，稱孝元傅皇后雲。

translations.literal: She died in the first year of Yuanshou; she was jointly buried at Weiling; she was titled Empress Fu of Emperor Xiaoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: She died in Yuanshou 1 (2 BCE) and was buried with Yuan at Weiling as his empress Fu.

sentences.zh: 定陶丁姬

translations.literal: Lady Ding of Dingtao.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ding of Dingtao.

sentences.zh: 定陶丁姬，哀帝母也，《易》祖師丁將軍之玄孫。

translations.literal: Lady Ding of Dingtao was Emperor Ai's mother; she was the great-great-granddaughter of General Ding, founding master of the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ding of Dingtao, Emperor Ai's mother, traced her line to General Ding Kuan, the Han master of the Changes.

sentences.zh: 家在山陽瑕丘，父至廬江太守。

translations.literal: Her family was in Xiaqiu of Shanyang; her father rose to governor of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Her people came from Xiaqiu in Shanyang; her father became governor of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 始，定陶恭王先為山陽王，而丁氏內其女為姬。

translations.literal: At first King Gong of Dingtao had first been King of Shanyang; and the Ding clan brought in their daughter as concubine.
translations.idiomatic: When the future King Gong still ruled Shanyang, the Ding family sent her in as his concubine.

sentences.zh: 王后姓張氏，其母鄭禮，即傅太后同母弟也。

translations.literal: The queen consort was surnamed Zhang; her mother was Zheng Li—she was Grand Empress Dowager Fu's uterine younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: The principal queen was a Zhang whose mother was Zheng Li—Lady Fu's half-brother.

sentences.zh: 太后以親戚故，欲其有子，然終無有。

translations.literal: The empress dowager because of kinship wished her to have children; yet in the end she had none.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Fu hoped her kinswoman would bear an heir, but she remained childless.

sentences.zh: 唯丁姬河平四年生哀帝。

translations.literal: Only Lady Ding in the fourth year of Heping bore Emperor Ai.
translations.idiomatic: Only Lady Ding gave birth—to Ai—in Heping 4 (25 BCE).

sentences.zh: 丁姬為帝太后，兩兄忠、明。

translations.literal: Lady Ding became Empress Dowager of the Emperor; she had two elder brothers Zhong and Ming.
translations.idiomatic: As empress dowager she had two brothers, Zhong and Ming.

sentences.zh: 明以帝舅封陽安侯。

translations.literal: Ming by virtue of being the emperor's maternal uncle was enfeoffed Marquis of Yang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ming became Marquis of Yang'an as the emperor's uncle.

sentences.zh: 忠蚤死，封忠子滿為平周侯。

translations.literal: Zhong died early; Zhong's son Man was enfeoffed Marquis of Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong died young; his son Man inherited the marquisate of Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 太后叔父憲、望，望為左將軍，憲為太僕。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's uncles Xian and Wang; Wang was left general; Xian was grand coachman.
translations.idiomatic: Her uncles Xian and Wang became grand coachman and left general respectively.

sentences.zh: 明為大司馬票騎將軍，輔政。

translations.literal: Ming was grand marshal and general of agile cavalry; he assisted government.
translations.idiomatic: Ming served as regent with the titles of grand marshal and general of agile cavalry.

sentences.zh: 丁氏侯者凡二人，大司馬一人，將軍、九卿、二千石六人，侍中、諸曹亦十餘人。

translations.literal: Those of the Ding clan who were marquises numbered two in all; grand marshal one; generals, nine ministers, and two-thousand-shi six; gentlemen-in-waiting and bureau heads likewise over ten.
translations.idiomatic: The Ding held two marquisates, one grand marshal, six senior posts, and a dozen court offices.

sentences.zh: 丁、傅以一二年間暴興尤盛。

translations.literal: Ding and Fu in one or two years violently rose especially flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: The Ding and Fu clans shot to power within a year or two.

sentences.zh: 然哀帝不甚假以權勢，權勢不如王氏在成帝世也。

translations.literal: Yet Emperor Ai did not greatly lend them power and influence; their power and influence did not match the Wang clan in Emperor Cheng's age.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ai never gave them the leverage the Wangs had enjoyed under Cheng.

sentences.zh: 建平二年，丁太后崩。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianping, Empress Dowager Ding died.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianping 2 (5 BCE) Empress Dowager Ding died.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「《詩》云『谷則異室，死則同穴』。

translations.literal: The sovereign said: 'The Odes say, "In life different chambers; in death the same pit."'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor quoted the Odes: "We dwelt apart in life—let us share one grave in death."

sentences.zh: 昔季武子成寢，杜氏之墓在西階下，請合葬而許之。

translations.literal: Formerly Ji Wuzi completed the sleeping hall; the Du clan's grave was below the west steps; he requested joint burial and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji Wuzi built his hall the Du family tomb lay beneath his western steps—he asked to bury his wife beside them and was granted leave.

sentences.zh: 附葬之禮，自周興焉。

translations.literal: The ritual of attached burial arose from Zhou onward.
translations.idiomatic: Joint burial has been orthodox since Zhou.

sentences.zh: 孝子事亡如事存，帝太后宜起陵恭皇之園。

translations.literal: The filial son serves the dead as serving the living—Empress Dowager of the Emperor ought raise a tumulus in Gong Emperor's garden park.'
translations.idiomatic: A dutiful son honors the dead as the living—lay Empress Dowager Ding's mausoleum in Emperor Gong's tomb park."

sentences.zh: 」遣大司馬票騎將軍明，東送葬於定陶，貴震山東。

translations.literal: He dispatched Grand Marshal and General of Agile Cavalry Ming to escort east for burial at Dingtao; nobility shook Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Ming east as grand marshal to bury her at Dingtao with pomp that shook the eastern provinces.

sentences.zh: 哀帝崩，王莽秉政，使有司舉奏丁、傅罪惡。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ai died, Wang Mang held government; he ordered offices to raise and memorialize Ding and Fu crimes.
translations.idiomatic: After Ai died Wang Mang ordered indictments of the Ding and Fu clans.

sentences.zh: 莽以太皇太后詔皆免官爵，丁氏徙歸故郡。

translations.literal: Mang by Grand Empress Dowager edict dismissed all from office and rank; the Ding clan was moved back to their native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Acting for Grand Empress Dowager Wang he stripped their titles and sent the Dings home.

sentences.zh: 莽奏貶傅太后號為定陶恭王母，丁太后號曰丁姬。

translations.literal: Mang memorialized demoting Grand Empress Dowager Fu's title to mother of King Gong of Dingtao; Empress Dowager Ding's title to Lady Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He reduced Fu to "mother of King Gong of Dingtao" and Ding to plain Lady Ding.

sentences.zh: 元始五年，莽復言：「恭王母、丁姬前不臣妾，至葬渭陵，塚高與元帝山齊，懷帝太后、皇太太后璽綬以葬，不應禮。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanshi, Mang again said: 'Gong King's mother and Lady Ding formerly did not submit as concubines; reaching burial at Weiling, mound height matched Yuan Emperor's hill; bearing Empress Dowager of the Emperor and Grand Empress Dowager Supreme seals and ribbons to bury—this does not accord with ritual.'
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanshi 5 (5 CE) Wang Mang charged that Fu and Ding had refused humble rank yet were buried at Weiling beside Yuan with imperial seals—that violated every rule.

sentences.zh: 禮有改葬，請發恭王母及丁姬塚，取其璽綬消滅，徙恭王母及丁姬歸定陶，葬恭王塚次，而葬丁姬復其故。

translations.literal: Ritual allows reburial—your servant requests opening Gong King's mother's and Lady Ding's tombs, taking their seals and ribbons and destroying them, moving Gong King's mother and Lady Ding back to Dingtao, burying Gong King's mother beside King Gong's mound, while burying Lady Ding restoring her former status.'
translations.idiomatic: Rites permitted reburial; he asked to open their tombs, melt the seals, return Fu and Ding to Dingtao—Fu beside Emperor Gong's mound and Ding in her original modest grave.

sentences.zh: 」太后以為既已之事，不須復發。

translations.literal: The empress dowager held that since it was already done, it need not be reopened.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Empress Dowager Wang thought the dead should rest undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 莽固爭之，太后詔曰：「因故棺為致槨作塚，祠以太牢。

translations.literal: Mang firmly contested it; the empress dowager edicted: 'Using the old inner coffin make an outer shell and mound; sacrifice with grand beast.'
translations.idiomatic: Mang insisted until she authorized new outer coffins and taishao offerings.

sentences.zh: 」謁者護既發傅太后塚，崩壓殺數百人；

translations.literal: When usher-guards had opened Grand Empress Dowager Fu's tomb, collapse crushed and killed several hundred;
translations.idiomatic: When they broke into Fu's tomb the vault collapsed and killed hundreds;

sentences.zh: 開丁姬槨戶，火出炎四五丈，吏卒以水沃滅乃得入，燒燔槨中器物。

translations.literal: opening Lady Ding's outer coffin door, fire issued flames four or five zhang; clerks and soldiers poured water to extinguish before they could enter; it burned and charred objects inside the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: opening Ding's sarcophagus unleashed a pillar of flame; crews had to flood it before entering, by which time the grave goods were ash.

sentences.zh: 莽復奏言：「前恭王母生，僭居桂宮，皇天震怒，災其正殿；

translations.literal: Mang again memorialized: 'Formerly Gong King's mother while alive overstepped dwelling in Cassia Palace; august Heaven shook with anger and disaster struck its main hall;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang added that while Fu lived she usurped Cassia Palace until Heaven blasted its main hall;

sentences.zh: 丁姬死，葬逾制度，今火焚其槨，此天見變以告，當改如媵妾也。

translations.literal: Lady Ding died; burial exceeded regulation; now fire burned her outer coffin—this is Heaven showing transformation to announce—ought to be changed like concubine-handmaid.'
translations.idiomatic: Ding's overscale tomb now burst into flame—Heaven itself demands she be buried as a mere concubine.

sentences.zh: 臣前奏請葬丁姬復故，非是。

translations.literal: Your servant's former memorial requesting burying Lady Ding restoring her former status—was not correct.'
translations.idiomatic: His earlier plan to rebury Ding in her old plot was wrong.

sentences.zh: 恭王母及丁姬棺皆名梓宮，珠玉之衣非籓妾服，請更以木棺代，去珠玉衣，葬丁姬媵妾之次。

translations.literal: Gong King's mother's and Lady Ding's coffins were both named catalpa palace coffins; pearl-jade shrouds are not vassal concubine dress—your servant requests replacing with wooden coffins instead, removing pearl-jade shrouds, burying Lady Ding in concubine-handmaid station.'
translations.idiomatic: Both women lay in imperial catalpa coffins wearing jade shrouds—replace them with plain wood, strip the shrouds, and inter Ding among secondary wives.

sentences.zh: 」奏可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne assented.

sentences.zh: 既開傅太后棺，臭聞數里。

translations.literal: Once Grand Empress Dowager Fu's coffin was opened, stench was heard for several li.
translations.idiomatic: Opening Fu's coffin released a stench for miles.

sentences.zh: 公卿在位皆阿莽指，入錢帛，遣子弟及諸生四夷，凡十餘萬人，操持作具，助將作掘平恭王母、丁姬故塚，二旬間皆平。

translations.literal: Dukes and ministers in office all flattered Mang's intent; contributing cash and silk, dispatching sons and younger brothers and scholars to the four barbarians—in all over a hundred thousand people, wielding work tools, assisting the master of works in digging level Gong King's mother's and Lady Ding's old tombs; within twenty days all were leveled.
translations.idiomatic: The whole bureaucracy toadied to Mang, sent cash, and drafted more than a hundred thousand laborers to level Fu and Ding's mounds within twenty days.

sentences.zh: 莽又周棘其處以為世戒雲。

translations.literal: Mang also surrounded the place with thorns to be a warning to the age.
translations.idiomatic: He ringed the site with brambles as a lesson to posterity.

sentences.zh: 時有群燕數千，銜土投丁姬穿中。

translations.literal: At the time there was a flock of swallows several thousand; carrying mud they cast it into Lady Ding's pit.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of swallows were seen dropping mud into Ding's open grave.

sentences.zh: 丁、傅既敗，孔鄉侯晏將家屬徙合浦，宗族皆歸故郡。

translations.literal: Once Ding and Fu had fallen, Marquis of Kongxiang Yan led household dependents moved to Hepu; the lineage kin all returned to native commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: When the clans fell, Yan of Kongxiang was banished to Hepu while kin scattered home.

sentences.zh: 唯高武侯喜得全，自有傳。

translations.literal: Only Marquis of Gaowu Xi obtained preservation intact—he has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Only Xi of Gaowu survived unscathed—his life is told elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 孝哀傅皇后

translations.literal: Empress Fu of Emperor Ai.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Fu of Emperor Ai.

sentences.zh: 孝哀傅皇后，定陶太后從弟子也。

translations.literal: Empress Fu of Emperor Ai was a niece of Grand Empress Dowager of Dingtao.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Fu was a niece of Lady Fu of Dingtao.

sentences.zh: 哀帝為定陶王時，傅太后欲重親，取以配王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ai was King of Dingtao, Grand Empress Dowager Fu wished to strengthen kinship ties; she took her to match the king.
translations.idiomatic: While Ai was still prince of Dingtao, Lady Fu married him to a kinswoman to tighten the family bond.

sentences.zh: 王入為漢太子，傅氏女為妃。

translations.literal: The king entered to become Han heir apparent; the Fu clan daughter became consort.
translations.idiomatic: When he became crown prince she followed as his consort.

sentences.zh: 哀帝即位，成帝大行尚在前殿，而傅太后封傅妃父晏為孔鄉侯，與帝舅陽安侯丁明同日俱封。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ai ascended the throne, Emperor Cheng's grand procession was still in the front hall; yet Grand Empress Dowager Fu enfeoffed Consort Fu's father Yan as Marquis of Kongxiang, together with the emperor's maternal uncle Marquis of Yang'an Ding Ming enfeoffed the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Ai had barely taken the throne while Cheng's bier still stood in the hall when Lady Fu ennobled her father Yan alongside the emperor's uncle Ding Ming.

sentences.zh: 時師丹諫，以為：「天下自王者所有，親戚何患不富貴？

translations.literal: At the time Shi Dan remonstrated, holding: 'All under Heaven belongs to the king—why worry that kin will not be rich and noble?'
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dan protested: "The realm is the emperor's—kin will prosper in due time without such haste."

sentences.zh: 而倉卒若是，其不久長矣！

translations.literal: Yet to be hasty like this—it will not last long!'
translations.idiomatic: Rewards thrown out this rashly will not endure!"

sentences.zh: 」晏封後月餘，傅妃立為皇后。

translations.literal: More than a month after Yan was enfeoffed, Consort Fu was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: A month after Yan's enfeoffment his daughter became empress.

sentences.zh: 傅氏既盛，晏最尊重。

translations.literal: Once the Fu clan flourished, Yan was most honored and weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Fu kin Yan stood highest.

sentences.zh: 哀帝崩，王莽白太皇太后下詔曰：「定陶恭王太后與孔鄉侯晏同心合謀，背恩忘本，專恣不軌，與至尊同稱號，終沒，至乃配食於左坐，悖逆無道。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ai died, Wang Mang reported to Grand Empress Dowager and issued an edict: 'Grand Empress Dowager of King Gong of Dingtao and Marquis of Kongxiang Yan joined hearts in plotting; they turned back on grace and forgot roots; they monopolized and indulged against the track; they shared titles with the supreme one; at final death they even received paired sacrifice at the left seat—rebellious and non-canonical.'
translations.idiomatic: After Ai died Wang Mang had Lady Fu and Yan indicted for conspiring against the throne, usurping imperial titles, and receiving sacrifices reserved for empresses.

sentences.zh: 今令孝哀皇后退就桂宮。

translations.literal: Now order Empress of Emperor Ai to withdraw to Cassia Palace.'
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Empress Fu confined to Cassia Palace.

sentences.zh: 」後月餘，復與孝成趙皇后俱廢為庶人，就其園自殺。

translations.literal: More than a month later, again together with Empress Zhao of Emperor Cheng she was both deposed as commoner; she went to her garden park and killed herself.'
translations.idiomatic: Within weeks she and Zhao Feiyan were stripped to commoners and driven to suicide in their tomb parks.

sentences.zh: 孝元馮昭儀

translations.literal: Lady Feng the Brilliant Companion of Emperor Xiaoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Feng, Brilliant Companion of Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 孝元馮昭儀，平帝祖母也。

translations.literal: Lady Feng the Brilliant Companion of Emperor Xiaoyuan was Emperor Ping's grandmother.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Feng was Emperor Ping's grandmother.

sentences.zh: 元帝即位二年，以選入後宮。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Yuan's reign she was selected and entered the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: She entered the harem in the second year of Yuan's reign.

sentences.zh: 時父奉世為執金吾。

translations.literal: At the time her father Feng Shi was Bearer of the Mace.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Feng Shi then served as Bearer of the Mace.

sentences.zh: 昭儀始為長使，數月至美人，後五年就館生男，拜為婕妤。

translations.literal: The Brilliant Companion began as senior attendant; within several months she became Fair Lady; after five years she went to the lying-in quarters and bore a son; she was appointed Favorite Beauty.
translations.idiomatic: She rose from senior attendant to Fair Lady within months; five years later she bore a son in the birthing lodge and was named Favorite Beauty.

sentences.zh: 時父奉世為右將軍光祿勳，奉世長男野王為左馮翊，父子並居朝廷，議者以為器能當其位，非用女寵故也。

translations.literal: At the time her father Feng Shi was right general and superintendent of the Imperial Household; Feng Shi's eldest son Yewang was left administrator of Fengyi; father and son together occupied the court—those who discussed it held that talent matched their positions, not because of employment of female favor.
translations.idiomatic: By then her father was right general and superintendent of the household; her brother Yewang governed Fengyi—commentators said merit, not nepotism through the harem, had won those posts.

sentences.zh: 而馮婕妤內寵與傅昭儀等。

translations.literal: But Lady Feng the Favorite Beauty's inner favor was equal to Fu the Brilliant Companion's.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Feng stood in Cheng's affection beside Lady Fu the Brilliant Companion.

sentences.zh: 建昭中，上幸虎圈鬥獸，後宮皆坐。

translations.literal: In the Jianzhao era the sovereign visited the tiger pit beast combat; the rear palace all sat.
translations.idiomatic: During Jianzhao Yuan watched beast fights at the tiger pit while the harem looked on.

sentences.zh: 熊佚出圈，攀檻欲上殿。

translations.literal: A bear escaped the pen, climbed the railing wishing to ascend the hall.
translations.idiomatic: A bear broke loose, clawed the rail, and tried to rush the dais.

sentences.zh: 左右貴人傅昭儀等皆驚走，馮婕妤直前當熊而立，左右格殺熊。

translations.literal: Attendant noblewomen Fu the Brilliant Companion and others all fled in alarm; Lady Feng the Favorite Beauty went straight forward and stood blocking the bear; attendants struck and killed the bear.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Fu and the others fled; Lady Feng stepped in front of the beast until guards brought it down.

sentences.zh: 上問：「人情驚懼，何故前當熊？

translations.literal: The sovereign asked: 'Human feeling is alarm and fear—why did you advance to block the bear?'
translations.idiomatic: He asked why she alone had stepped toward the danger.

sentences.zh: 」婕妤對曰：「猛獸得人而止，妾恐熊至御坐，故以身當之。

translations.literal: The Favorite Beauty replied: 'Fierce beasts stop when they have caught a person—your servant feared the bear would reach the imperial seat; therefore she used her body to block it.'
translations.idiomatic: She answered, "Beasts halt once they seize prey—I feared it would reach your throne, so I stood in its path."

sentences.zh: 」元帝嗟歎，以此倍敬重焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan sighed in admiration; for this reason he doubly respected and honored her.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan marveled and honored her twice over.

sentences.zh: 傅昭儀等皆慚。

translations.literal: Fu the Brilliant Companion and others were all ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Fu and the rest were mortified.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，馮婕妤男立為信都王，尊婕妤為昭儀。

translations.literal: The next summer, Lady Feng the Favorite Beauty's son was established as King of Xindu; she was honored as Brilliant Companion.
translations.idiomatic: The next summer her son was made king of Xindu and she was raised to Brilliant Companion.

sentences.zh: 元帝崩，為信都太后，與王俱居儲元宮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan died, she became Grand Empress Dowager of Xindu; together with the king she dwelt in Chuyuan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan died she became dowager of Xindu and lived with her son in Chuyuan Palace.

sentences.zh: 河平中，隨王之國。

translations.literal: In the Heping era she followed the king to his kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: During Heping she followed him to his fief.

sentences.zh: 後徙中山，是為孝王。

translations.literal: Later he was moved to Zhongshan—this was King Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to Zhongshan and posthumously styled King Xiao.

sentences.zh: 後征定陶王為太子，封中山王舅參為宜鄉侯。

translations.literal: Later the King of Dingtao was summoned as heir apparent; the King of Zhongshan's maternal uncle Shen was enfeoffed Marquis of Yixiang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Dingtao prince became heir, Lady Feng's brother Shen was ennobled as Marquis of Yixiang.

sentences.zh: 參，馮太后少弟也。

translations.literal: Shen was Grand Empress Dowager Feng's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was her younger brother.

sentences.zh: 是歲，孝王薨，有一男，嗣為王，時未滿歲，有眚病，太后自養視，數禱祠解。

translations.literal: That year King Xiao died; he had one boy who succeeded as king; at the time not yet full year of age, he had injurious illness; the grand empress dowager personally reared and watched over him, repeatedly praying and sacrificing to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: That year King Xiao left an infant heir plagued by ill omens; Lady Feng nursed him herself and offered prayer after prayer for his recovery.

sentences.zh: 哀帝即位，遣中郎謁者張由將醫治中山小王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ai ascended the throne, he dispatched gentleman of the interior usher Zhang You to lead physicians to treat the young King of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Ai sent Zhang You with physicians to treat the young king of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 由素有狂易病，病發怒去，西歸長安。

translations.literal: You had long had manic illness; when the illness flared he angrily departed and returned west to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang You was mentally unstable; in a fit he abandoned his post and fled to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 尚書簿責擅去狀，由恐，因誣言中山太后祝詛上及太后。

translations.literal: The imperial secretary ledger-reprimanded the circumstance of leaving without authority; You feared and thereupon falsely said Grand Empress Dowager of Zhongshan prayed and cursed the sovereign and the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The secretariat called him to account; panicking, he accused Lady Feng of cursing the emperor and empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 太后即傅昭儀也，素常怨馮太后，因是遣御史丁玄案驗，盡收御者官吏及馮氏昆弟在國者百餘人，分系雒陽、魏郡、巨鹿。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was Fu the Brilliant Companion; she had always resented Grand Empress Dowager Feng; on this account she dispatched imperial clerk Ding Xuan to investigate and verify; she wholly seized chariot-drivers, officials, and Feng clan brothers in the kingdom over a hundred persons, separately imprisoned at Luoyang, Wei, and Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Fu, who had long hated Lady Feng, sent Ding Xuan to investigate; more than a hundred Feng kin and officials were jailed across three commanderies.

sentences.zh: 數十日無所得，更使中謁者令史立與丞相長史、大鴻臚丞雜治。

translations.literal: Several tens of days brought nothing obtained; she further ordered palace usher director Shi Li together with the chancellor's chief clerk and grand herald assistant jointly to try the case.
translations.idiomatic: After weeks without proof she handed the case to Shi Li and senior ministers for joint trial.

sentences.zh: 立受傅太后指，幾得封侯，治馮太后女弟習及寡弟婦君之，死者數十人。

translations.literal: Li received Grand Empress Dowager Fu's intent; he nearly obtained enfeoffment as marquis; he tried Grand Empress Dowager Feng's younger sister Xi and her widowed younger brother's wife Junzhi—several tens died.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Li, hoping for a marquisate from Lady Fu, tortured Lady Feng's sister Xi and her sister-in-law Junzhi until dozens lay dead.

sentences.zh: 巫劉吾服祝詛。

translations.literal: Wu Liu Wu confessed to prayer-cursing.
translations.idiomatic: The witch Liu Wu confessed to cursing the throne.

sentences.zh: 醫徐遂成言習、君之曰：「武帝時醫修氏剌治武帝得二千萬耳，今愈上，不得封侯，不如殺上，令中山王代，可得封。

translations.literal: Physician Xu Suicheng said Xi and Junzhi said: 'In Emperor Wu's time physician Xiu clan lanced-treated Emperor Wu and got twenty million cash only; now curing the sovereign, not obtaining enfeoffment as marquis—better kill the sovereign and order the King of Zhongshan to succeed—then one can obtain enfeoffment.'
translations.idiomatic: Xu Suicheng claimed Xi and Junzhi had said court physicians once earned millions lancing Emperor Wu—if curing the present emperor won no marquisate, better murder him and put the Zhongshan prince on the throne.

sentences.zh: 」立等劾奏祝詛謀反，大逆。

translations.literal: Li and others impeached and memorialized prayer-cursing and plotting rebellion—great treason.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Li memorialized treason and witchcraft.

sentences.zh: 責問馮太后，無服辭。

translations.literal: They pressed Grand Empress Dowager Feng with questions; she had no confessing words.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Feng admitted nothing under interrogation.

sentences.zh: 立曰：「熊之上殿何其勇，今何怯也！

translations.literal: Li said: 'Going up to the hall against the bear—how brave! Why so timid now!'
translations.idiomatic: Shi Li sneered, "You faced a bear on the steps—why so timid today?"

sentences.zh: 」太后還謂左右：「此乃中語，前世事，吏何用知之？

translations.literal: The grand empress dowager turned and said to those around her: 'This is inner speech, affairs of a former age—what use have clerks in knowing it?'
translations.idiomatic: She told her attendants, "Those were palace whispers from another reign—how would petty clerks know them?"

sentences.zh: 是欲陷我效也！

translations.literal: This is wishing to trap me with effect!'
translations.idiomatic: They mean to frame me!"

sentences.zh: 」乃飲藥自殺。

translations.literal: Thereupon she drank medicine and killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: She took poison.

sentences.zh: 先未死，有司請誅之，上不忍致法，廢為庶人，徙雲陽宮。

translations.literal: Before she had died, offices requested executing her; the sovereign could not bear to apply law; she was deposed as commoner and moved to Yunyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Before her death officials had sought execution; Ai commuted the sentence to commoner status and exile at Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 既死，有司復奏：「太后死在未廢前。

translations.literal: Once dead, offices again memorialized: 'The grand empress dowager died before being deposed.'
translations.idiomatic: After she died officials noted she had perished before deposition.

sentences.zh: 」有詔以諸侯王太后儀葬之。

translations.literal: There was an edict to bury her with feudal king grand empress dowager rites.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted her burial as a king's mother.

sentences.zh: 宜鄉侯參、君之、習夫及子當相坐者，或自殺，或伏法。

translations.literal: Marquis of Yixiang Shen, Junzhi, Xi's husband and sons who ought to sit mutual guilt—some killed themselves, some submitted to law.
translations.idiomatic: Shen, Junzhi, Xi's family, and others implicated died by suicide or execution.

sentences.zh: 參女弁為孝王后，有兩女，有司奏免為庶人，與馮氏宗族徙歸故郡。

translations.literal: Shen's daughter Bian was King Xiao's queen; she had two daughters; offices memorialized dismissing her as commoner; together with the Feng lineage kin she was moved back to native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shen's daughter, queen at Zhongshan, was reduced to commoner rank and the Feng clan sent home.

sentences.zh: 張由以先告賜爵關內侯，史立遷中太僕。

translations.literal: Zhang You for first reporting was granted rank of secondary marquis; Shi Li was promoted to palace grand coachman.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang You was ennobled for his accusation; Shi Li was promoted to grand coachman.

sentences.zh: 哀帝崩，大司徒孔光奏「由前誣告骨肉，立陷人入大辟，為國家結怨於天下，以取秩遷，獲爵邑，幸蒙赦令，請免為庶人，徒合浦」云。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ai died, Grand Minister of Education Kong Guang memorialized: 'You formerly falsely accused bone and flesh; Li trapped people into great death penalty; for the state he tied resentment under Heaven—to obtain rank promotion, obtain noble rank and fief; fortunately covered by amnesty edict—request dismissal as commoner, exile to Hepu.'
translations.idiomatic: After Ai died Kong Guang impeached Zhang You and Shi Li for framing kin and seeking promotion through bloodshed, asking that they be stripped and banished to Hepu.

sentences.zh: 中山衛姬

translations.literal: Lady Wei of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wei of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 中山衛姬，平帝母也。

translations.literal: Lady Wei of Zhongshan was Emperor Ping's mother.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wei of Zhongshan was Emperor Ping's mother.

sentences.zh: 父子豪，中山盧奴人，官至衛尉。

translations.literal: Her father Zihao was a man of Lunu in Zhongshan; his office reached commandant of the guards.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Wei Zihao of Lunu rose to commandant of the guards.

sentences.zh: 子豪女弟為宣帝婕妤，生楚孝王；

translations.literal: Zihao's younger sister was Emperor Xuan's Favorite Beauty; she bore King Xiao of Chu;
translations.idiomatic: His sister had been a Favorite Beauty of Emperor Xuan and mother of the king of Chu;

sentences.zh: 長女又為元帝婕妤，生平陽公主。

translations.literal: the eldest daughter again was Emperor Yuan's Favorite Beauty; she bore Princess Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: his eldest daughter became Yuan's Favorite Beauty and bore Princess Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 成帝時，中山孝王無子，上以衛氏吉祥，以子豪少女配孝王。

translations.literal: In Emperor Cheng's time King Xiao of Zhongshan had no son; the sovereign held the Wei clan auspicious; he matched Zihao's youngest daughter to King Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongshan lacked an heir Cheng married Wei Zihao's youngest daughter to the king as a lucky match.

sentences.zh: 元延四年，生平帝。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanyan she bore Emperor Ping.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Ping in Yuanyan 4 (9 BCE).

sentences.zh: 平帝年二歲，孝王薨，代為王。

translations.literal: Emperor Ping was two years old; King Xiao died; he succeeded as king.
translations.idiomatic: Ping was two when King Xiao died and the boy inherited the throne.

sentences.zh: 哀帝崩，無嗣。

translations.literal: Emperor Ai died; there was no heir.
translations.idiomatic: Ai died without an heir.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后與新都侯莽迎中山王立為帝。

translations.literal: Grand Empress Dowager together with Marquis of Xindu Mang welcomed the King of Zhongshan and established him as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Empress Dowager Wang and Wang Mang of Xindu raised the Zhongshan prince to the throne.

sentences.zh: 莽欲顓國權，懲丁、傅行事，以帝為成帝后，母衛姬及外家不當得至京師。

translations.literal: Mang wished to monopolize state power; taking warning from Ding and Fu's conduct; he made the emperor heir to Emperor Cheng; mother Lady Wei and outer kin ought not obtain access to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Mang meant to monopolize power; remembering the Ding and Fu clans, he styled Ping as Cheng's heir and barred Lady Wei and her kin from the capital.

sentences.zh: 乃更立宗室桃鄉侯子成都為中山王，奉孝王後，遣少傅左將軍甄豐賜衛姬璽綬，即拜為中山孝王后，以苦陘縣為湯沐邑。

translations.literal: Thereupon he further established imperial clansman the Marquis of Taoxiang's son Chengdu as King of Zhongshan to serve King Xiao's posterity; he dispatched junior tutor left general Zhen Feng to bestow Lady Wei seals and ribbons; immediately appointing her Grand Empress Dowager of Zhongshan Xiao; taking Ku County as bath-and-wash fief.
translations.idiomatic: He installed another prince at Zhongshan, sent Zhen Feng to invest Lady Wei as dowager with Ku county as her maintenance fief.

sentences.zh: 又賜帝舅衛寶、寶弟玄爵關內侯。

translations.literal: He also granted the emperor's maternal uncle Wei Bao and Bao's younger brother Xuan rank of secondary marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He ennobled Wei's brothers Bao and Xuan as secondary marquises.

sentences.zh: 賜帝三妹，謁臣號修義君，哉皮為承禮君，鬲子為尊德君，食邑各二千戶。

translations.literal: He granted the emperor's three younger sisters: Yechen titled Lady Xiuyi, Zaipi titled Lady Chengli, Gezi titled Lady Zunde—food fiefs each two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Ping's three sisters received titles as noble ladies with two-thousand-household fiefs.

sentences.zh: 莽長子宇非莽隔絕衛氏，恐久後受禍，即私與衛寶通書記，教衛後上書謝恩，因陳丁、傅舊惡，幾得至京師。

translations.literal: Mang's eldest son Yu faulted Mang for isolating the Wei clan; fearing long afterward receiving disaster; he privately exchanged letters with Wei Bao; he instructed Queen Wei to submit memorial thanking grace; thereby stating Ding and Fu old evils—almost succeeded in reaching the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu, fearing Mang's isolation of the Weis would bring disaster, secretly urged Lady Wei to memorialize thanks and cite the old Ding–Fu crimes—nearly winning a visit to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 莽白太皇太后詔有司曰：「中山孝王后深分明為人後之義，條陳故定陶傅太后、丁姬悖天逆理，上僭位號，徙定陶王於信都，為恭王立廟於京師，如天子制，不畏天命，侮聖人言，壞亂法度，居非其制，稱非其號。

translations.literal: Mang reported to Grand Empress Dowager and ordered offices: 'Grand Empress Dowager of Zhongshan Xiao deeply understands clear meaning of being another's heir; itemizes former Dingtao Grand Empress Dowager Fu, Ding Ji rebel against Heaven and invert principle, overstepping titles; moved King of Dingtao to Xindu; for Gong King established temple in capital like Son of Heaven system; not fearing Heaven's mandate; insulting sage men's words; wrecking and disordering laws and measures; dwelling not in their regulation; titling not their titles.'
translations.idiomatic: Mang had Grand Empress Dowager Wang praise Lady Wei for denouncing the late Fu and Ding affines for usurping ritual and bringing Heaven's fire on the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 是以皇天震怒，火燒其殿，六年之間大命不遂，禍殃仍重，竟令孝哀帝受其餘災，大失天心，夭命暴崩，又令恭王祭祀絕廢，精魂無所依歸。

translations.literal: Therefore august Heaven shook with anger; fire burned their halls; within six years the great mandate did not succeed; calamity and bane still heavy—ultimately causing Emperor Ai to receive their remaining disaster; greatly losing Heaven's heart; early mandate sudden collapse; again causing King Gong's sacrifices to be cut off and abandoned—spirit essences have nowhere to rely and return.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven had burned their halls, cut short Ai's life, and left Emperor Gong's spirit without offerings.

sentences.zh: 朕惟孝王后深說經義，明鏡聖法，懼古人之禍敗，近事之咎殃，畏天命，奉聖言，是乃久保一國，長獲天祿，而令孝王永享無疆之祀，福祥之大者也。

translations.literal: We consider that Grand Empress Dowager Xiao deeply expounds classic meaning; bright mirror to sage law; fears ancients' calamity and defeat; recent affairs' fault and disaster; fears Heaven's mandate; obeys sage words—this is then long preserving one kingdom, long obtaining Heaven's emolument, and causing King Xiao forever to enjoy boundless sacrifice—greatness of blessing and auspice.'
translations.idiomatic: The edict praised her grasp of the classics and promise of lasting fortune for Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: We greatly approve it.'
translations.idiomatic: The court applauded her wisdom.

sentences.zh: 夫褒義賞善，聖王之制，其以中山故安戶七千益中山後湯沐邑，加賜及中山王黃金各百斤，增傅相以下秩。」

translations.literal: Now praising righteousness and rewarding good is sage king's system; take Zhongshan's former seven thousand An households to augment Zhongshan posterity's bath-and-wash fief; add gift reaching King of Zhongshan yellow gold one hundred jin each; increase tutor and chancellor and below rank.'
translations.idiomatic: It granted seven thousand extra households to her fief, a hundred jin of gold to her and the king, and raised official salaries.

sentences.zh: 衛后日夜啼泣，思見帝，而但益戶邑。

translations.literal: Queen Wei day and night wept and cried, thinking to see the emperor; but only household fief was increased.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wei wept night and day to see her son but received only larger fiefs.

sentences.zh: 宇復教令上書求至京師。

translations.literal: Yu again instructed ordering memorial seeking to reach the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu again urged her to petition for entry to the capital.

sentences.zh: 會事發覺，莽殺宇，盡誅衛氏支屬。

translations.literal: When the affair was discovered, Mang killed Yu; he wholly executed Wei clan branch kin.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot surfaced Mang executed Yu and extirpated the Wei kin.

sentences.zh: 衛寶女為中山王后，免后，徙合浦。

translations.literal: Wei Bao's daughter was Queen of Zhongshan; she was dismissed from queen; moved to Hepu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's niece lost her queenship and was banished to Hepu.

sentences.zh: 唯衛后在，王莽篡國，廢為家人，后歲余卒，葬孝王旁。

translations.literal: Only Queen Wei remained; Wang Mang usurped the state; she was deposed as common person; after a bit over a year the queen died; buried beside King Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wei alone survived until Mang's usurpation; stripped of title she died a year later and was buried beside King Xiao.

sentences.zh: 孝平王皇后

translations.literal: Empress Wang of Emperor Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wang of Emperor Ping.

sentences.zh: 孝平王皇后，安漢公太傅大司馬莽女也。

translations.literal: Empress Wang of Emperor Ping was the daughter of Duke of Pacifying Han, grand tutor and grand marshal Mang.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wang was the daughter of Wang Mang, styled Duke of Pacifying Han.

sentences.zh: 平帝即位，年九歲，成帝母太皇太后稱制，而莽秉政。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ping ascended the throne, he was nine years old; Emperor Cheng's mother Grand Empress Dowager held the regency, while Mang grasped government.
translations.idiomatic: Ping came to the throne at nine under Grand Empress Dowager Wang with Mang holding real power.

sentences.zh: 莽欲依霍光故事，以女配帝，太后意不欲也。

translations.literal: Mang wished to follow Huo Guang's precedent, matching his daughter to the emperor; the empress dowager's intent did not wish it.
translations.idiomatic: Mang sought to imitate Huo Guang by marrying his daughter to the boy emperor; the grand empress dowager resisted.

sentences.zh: 莽設變詐，令女必入，因以自重，事在《莽傳》。

translations.literal: Mang set up shifts and deceit, causing the daughter necessarily to enter; thereby to weight himself—the affair is in the 'Biography of Mang.'
translations.idiomatic: Mang schemed until the match was fixed; the full intrigue is told in his biography.

sentences.zh: 太后不得已而許之，遣長樂少府夏侯籓、宗正劉宏、少府宗伯鳳、尚書令平晏納采、太師光、大司徒馬宮、大司空甄豐、左將軍孫建、執金吾尹賞、行太常事太中大夫劉歆及太卜、太史令以下四十九人賜皮弁素績，以禮雜卜筮，太牢祠宗廟，待吉月日。

translations.literal: The grand empress dowager had no choice but to consent; she dispatched the superintendent of Changle Xia Hou Fan, the director of the imperial clan Liu Hong, the privy treasurer Zong Bo Feng, the supervisor of the masters of writing Ping Yan, and others to conduct the betrothal gifts ceremony—Grand Tutor Guang, Grand Minister of Education Ma Gong, Grand Minister of Works Zhen Feng, Left General Sun Jian, Bearer of the Mace Yin Shang, and Attendant Grandee Liu Xin acting for the grand master of ceremonies, together with the grand diviner, grand astrologer, and subordinates, forty-nine persons in all—who were granted leather caps and plain hemp skeins; by rite they combined milfoil and tortoise divination, sacrificed the highest offering at the ancestral temple, and awaited an auspicious month and day.
translations.idiomatic: She gave in and sent a party of forty-nine, from high ministers to diviners, capped and robed for the rite to take the betrothal omens, sacrifice at the ancestral temple, and set a wedding date.

sentences.zh: 明年春，遣大司徒宮、大司空豐、左將軍建、右將軍甄邯、光祿大夫歆奉乘輿法駕，迎皇后於安漢公第。

translations.literal: The next spring she dispatched Grand Minister of Education Gong, Grand Minister of Works Feng, Left General Jian, Right General Zhen Han, and Grand Counselor of the Household Xin, bearing the imperial carriage and full escort, to welcome the empress at the mansion of the Duke of An-Han.
translations.idiomatic: That spring Ma Gong, Zhen Feng, Sun Jian, Zhen Han, and Liu Xin went with the full imperial train to fetch the bride from Wang Mang’s ducal residence.

sentences.zh: 宮、豐、歆授皇后璽紱，登車稱警蹕，便時上林延壽門，入未央宮前殿。

translations.literal: Gong, Feng, and Xin handed the empress the seal-cord and ribbon; they mounted the carriage with the cleared-road escort called; at the appointed hour they entered by the Yanshou Gate of Shanglin and went into the front hall of Weiyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: They invested her with the empress’s seal, rolled out with full escort through Shanglin’s Yanshou Gate, and brought her into Weiyang’s main hall.

sentences.zh: 群臣就位行禮，大赦天下。

translations.literal: The host of ministers took their stations and performed the rites; there was a general amnesty for the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The court completed the ceremony and proclaimed an empire-wide amnesty.

sentences.zh: 益封父安漢公地滿百里，賜迎皇后及行禮者，自三公以下至騶宰執事長樂、未央宮、安漢公第者，皆增秩，賜金、帛各有差。

translations.literal: They added to the father's fief as Duke of An-Han until it reached a hundred li; those who welcomed the empress and performed the rites, from the three dukes down to grooms and stewards serving at Changle, Weiyang, and the Duke of An-Han's mansion, all had their ranks increased, and were granted gold and silk in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Mang’s father’s ducal estate was expanded to a full hundred li, and everyone involved in the wedding—from the three excellencies down to stable hands at the palaces—got a promotion and a share of gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 皇后立三月，以禮見高廟。

translations.literal: The empress having been established three months, by rite she appeared at the shrine to Emperor Gao.
