translations.idiomatic: Three months after her installation she paid formal homage at Gaozu's temple.

sentences.zh: 尊父安漢公號曰宰衡，位在諸侯王上。

translations.literal: They honored the father, the Duke of An-Han, with the title Regulator and Balance, his rank placed above the kings of the blood.
translations.idiomatic: Mang’s father was titled Regulator and Balance and ranked above the imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 賜公夫人號曰功顯君，食邑。

translations.literal: They granted the duke's consort the title Lady Merit-Illustrious, with a revenue district.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was styled Lady Merit-Illustrious with a sustaining fief.

sentences.zh: 封公子安為褒新侯，臨為賞都侯。

translations.literal: They enfeoffed the duke's sons An as marquis of Bao-Xin and Lin as marquis of Shang-Du.
translations.idiomatic: Mang’s brothers An and Lin were made marquises of Bao-Xin and Shang-Du.

sentences.zh: 后立歲餘，平帝崩。

translations.literal: The empress having been established a little over a year, Emperor Ping died.
translations.idiomatic: A year after the wedding Emperor Ping died.

sentences.zh: 莽立孝宣帝玄孫嬰為孺子，莽攝帝位，尊皇后為皇太后。

translations.literal: Mang established the great-great-grandson of Emperor Xuan, Ying, as heir-apparent; Mang held the imperial position in regency; they honored the empress as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Mang set the infant Liu Ying on the throne as puppet heir while he ruled as regent and elevated the empress to empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 三年，莽即真，以嬰為定安公，改皇太后號為定安公太后。

translations.literal: In the third year Mang assumed the true throne; he made Ying duke of Ding-An and changed the empress dowager's title to dowager of the duke of Ding-An.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later Wang Mang took the throne for real, demoted Ying to Duke of Ding-An, and restyled her as dowager of that petty dukedom.

sentences.zh: 太后時年十八矣，為人婉娩有節操。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was then eighteen years of age; in person she was gentle and yielding and had integrity of conduct.
translations.idiomatic: She was only eighteen, soft-spoken and principled.

sentences.zh: 自劉氏廢，常稱疾不朝會。

translations.literal: From the time the Liu house was cast aside, she constantly claimed illness and did not attend court assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: After the Han line was set aside she stayed away from court, pleading illness.

sentences.zh: 莽敬憚傷哀，欲嫁之，乃更號為黃皇室主，令立國將軍成新公孫建世子盛飾，將醫往問疾。

translations.literal: Mang respected, feared, and pitied her in her grief; wishing to marry her off, he then changed her title to Princess of the Yellow House; he ordered the Establish-the-State general, Duke of Cheng-Xin Sun Jian's heir, in full adornment, to lead physicians to go inquire after her illness.
translations.idiomatic: Mang pitied her and wanted her remarried; he restyled her Princess of the Yellow House and sent Sun Jian's son, the heir of the Duke of Cheng-Xin, dressed to the nines with physicians in tow, to call on her illness.

sentences.zh: 後大怒，笞鞭其旁侍御。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was greatly angered and flogged with a bamboo those attendants beside her.
translations.idiomatic: She flew into a rage and had the attendants at her side whipped.

sentences.zh: 因發病，不肯起，莽遂不復強也。

translations.literal: Thereupon she fell ill and would not rise; Mang then no longer pressed her.
translations.idiomatic: She took to her bed and refused to get up, and Mang finally stopped forcing the issue.

sentences.zh: 及漢兵誅莽，燔燒未央宮，後曰：「何面目以見漢家！

translations.literal: When Han troops executed Mang and set fire to Weiyang Palace, the empress said, "With what face am I to meet the house of Han!
translations.idiomatic: When Han forces killed Wang Mang and burned Weiyang Palace, she cried, "What face do I have left to show the Liu house!

sentences.zh: 」自投火中而死。

translations.literal: " She cast herself into the fire and died.
translations.idiomatic: " She leaped into the flames and died.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：《易》著吉凶而言謙盈之效，天地鬼神至於人道靡不同之。

translations.literal: The Appraisal says: The Changes records good and ill fortune and sets forth the efficacy of modesty versus fullness; from Heaven and Earth and the ghosts and spirits down to the way of mankind, there is none that does not accord with this.
translations.idiomatic: The summation: the Book of Changes ties fortune to humility and excess; the pattern runs from cosmos to commoner.

sentences.zh: 夫女寵之興，由至微而體至尊，窮富貴而不以功，此固道家所畏，禍福之宗也。

translations.literal: As for the rise of women's favor, from the most lowly they come to embody the most exalted; they exhaust wealth and honor without merit—this is indeed what the Daoists fear, the root of blessing and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Favored consorts climb from obscurity to the pinnacle yet owe nothing to merit; small wonder Daoist thought treats them as omens of rise and ruin.

sentences.zh: 序自漢興，終於孝平，外戚後庭色寵著聞二十有餘人，然其保位全家者，唯文、景、武帝太后及邛成後四人而已。

translations.literal: In the sequence from the rise of Han down to filial-ping, more than twenty women of the outer kin and rear palaces were renowned for beauty and favor; yet those who preserved their position and their whole families were only four: the empresses dowager of Wen, Jing, and Wu, and Empress Cheng of Qiong.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han began through Ping, over twenty imperial in-laws and inner-palace favorites made the chronicles, but only four—the dowagers of Wen, Jing, and Wu, plus Empress Cheng of Qiong—kept their houses intact.

sentences.zh: 至如史良娣、王悼後、許恭哀後身皆夭折不辜，而家依托舊恩，不敢縱恣，是以能全。

translations.literal: As for Concubine Shi, Empress Wang Dao, and Empress Xu Gong'ai, though their persons all met untimely deaths though innocent, their families relied on former grace and dared not give free rein, and thereby could be preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: Shi the heir's mother, Empress Wang Dao, and Empress Xu the Mourning died young and wronged, yet their kin clung to old favor and kept their heads down, so they survived.

sentences.zh: 其餘大者夷滅，小者放流，嗚呼！

translations.literal: Of the rest, the great clans were exterminated, the small were banished and cast out—alas!
translations.idiomatic: The rest were wiped out or driven into exile—alas!

sentences.zh: 鑒茲行事，變亦備矣。

translations.literal: Reflecting on these deeds carried out, the lesson of change is also complete.
translations.idiomatic: Read these stories and every turn of fortune is already spelled out.
